documents.title: How Verasist Works
documents.excerpt: The big picture — from API call to phone conversation to transcript
documents.content:
Verasist is a platform for building and running voice AI agents. You define a conversation flow, connect a phone number, and Verasist handles the rest — transcribing the caller's speech (STT), generating intelligent responses (LLM), speaking them back in a natural voice (TTS), and returning structured results when the call ends.

The core loop

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Dashboard / Your App
    participant API as Verasist API
    participant STT as Transcriber (STT)
    participant LLM as LLM Provider
    participant TTS as Voice Synthesizer (TTS)
    participant Tel as Telephony Provider
    participant Cal as Caller / Contact

U->>API: Trigger call (dashboard or API)
    API->>Tel: Initiate outbound call
    Tel->>Cal: Phone rings
    Cal-->>Tel: Answers
    Tel-->>API: Raw audio stream
    loop Conversation
        API->>STT: Caller audio
        STT-->>API: Transcribed text
        API->>LLM: Transcript + agent prompt + context
        LLM-->>API: Agent response text
        API->>TTS: Response text
        TTS-->>API: Synthesized audio
        API->>Tel: Audio stream
        Tel->>Cal: Agent speaks
    end
    API->>API: Extract context, run webhooks
    API-->>U: Run record (transcript, recording, gathered data)

Key components

Workflows (Agents) The conversation logic. A workflow is a graph of nodes (conversation steps) connected by edges (conditional transitions). You define what the agent says, when it moves on, and what data it collects.

Runs Every execution of a workflow creates a run. The run record holds the transcript, recording, extracted data, and cost information.

Telephony The phone infrastructure. Verasist connects to your telephony provider (Twilio, Vonage, etc.) to place and receive calls. The audio streams between the caller and Verasist in real time.

Transcriber (STT) Converts the caller's speech to text in real time. Verasist sends the audio stream to your configured speech-to-text provider and uses the transcript to drive both the LLM and the final run record.

LLM Provider Processes the transcript and the active node's prompt to generate the agent's next response. It also evaluates edge conditions to decide when to move the conversation forward.

Voice Synthesizer (TTS) Converts the LLM's text response to audio and streams it back to the caller. The choice of TTS provider and voice is configurable per agent.

How it fits together

When you trigger a call:

  1. Verasist instructs your telephony provider to dial the number
  2. When the caller answers, a real-time audio pipeline opens
  3. The caller's speech is transcribed by the STT provider
  4. The transcript is sent to the LLM with the active node's prompt and conversation history
  5. The LLM responds — the response is synthesized to audio by the TTS provider and streamed to the caller
  6. When an edge condition is met, Verasist transitions to the next node
  7. When an end node is reached, the call ends
  8. Post-call: context is extracted, webhooks fire, the run record is saved

Next steps

How the conversation graph works The lifecycle of a call How data flows through a conversation Running agents at scale

documents.title: Workflows & Agents
documents.excerpt: How conversation flows are defined in Verasist
documents.content:
In Verasist, what you see as an agent in the dashboard is called a workflow in the API. They are the same thing — a workflow is the underlying definition, agent is the product name for it.

Anywhere the API says workflow, think "agent". Anywhere the API says workflow_definition, think "the conversation logic inside your agent".

The graph model

A workflow is a directed graph — a set of nodes connected by edges.

graph LR
    A[Start Call] -->|Caller greets| B[Qualify Intent]
    B -->|Wants support| C[Support Agent]
    B -->|Wants sales| D[Sales Agent]
    C -->|Issue resolved| E[End Call]
    D -->|Demo booked| E

Nodes are the steps in the conversation. Each node has a prompt that tells the LLM what to say and do at that point.

Edges are the transitions between nodes. Each edge has a condition — a natural language description of when to move on. The LLM evaluates whether the condition has been met based on the conversation so far.

Node types

| Type | What it does | |---|---| | startCall | Entry point for telephony calls. The first thing the agent says when a call connects | | agentNode | An LLM-powered conversation step. The core building block | | globalNode | Defines instructions that apply across all agent nodes (e.g. tone, language, fallback behaviour) | | endCall | Terminates the call | | trigger | Entry point for API-triggered runs (non-telephony) | | webhook | Fires an HTTP request when reached — use for CRM updates, notifications, etc. | | qa | Runs automated quality analysis on the completed call |

Edges and transitions

An edge connects two nodes and fires when its condition is satisfied:

transition_speech is optional — if set, the agent speaks it before moving to the next node.

Versioning

Every time you update a workflow's workflow_definition, Verasist saves a new version while keeping the history. The current version is always what runs. Old versions are retained for auditing.

Creating workflows

There are two ways to create a workflow via the API:

  • From a definition — provide the full node/edge graph yourself. Best for programmatic generation.
  • From a template — describe the use case in natural language and Verasist generates the initial graph using an LLM. Best for getting started quickly.
See the Workflow Definition Schema for the full field reference.

documents.title: Calls & Runs
documents.excerpt: The lifecycle of a call and how runs capture its results
documents.content:
Every time a workflow executes, Verasist creates a run. The run is the record of that execution: what was said, what data was collected, how long it took, and what it cost.

Calls vs runs

A call is the audio connection — whether over the phone via a telephony provider, or through the browser via Web Call.

A run is the Verasist record of the workflow execution. Every call — outbound, inbound, web, or campaign — creates a run with the same contents: transcript, recording, gathered context, usage, and cost. Campaign runs are additionally linked to their parent campaign.

Call lifecycle

The call lifecycle tracks the telephony connection — from the moment a number is dialed to when the line drops.

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Ringing: Number dialed
    Ringing --> Connected: Caller answers
    Ringing --> Ended: No answer / voicemail
    Connected --> Ended: Conversation completes
    Connected --> Ended: Error or disconnect
    Ended --> [*]

For inbound calls, the flow starts when the caller dials in and the telephony provider routes the call to Verasist.

Inbound vs outbound

Outbound calls are initiated by Verasist — you trigger them via the API or dashboard with a phone number and agent. Used for proactive outreach, reminders, and campaigns.

Inbound calls are initiated by the caller — your telephony provider routes incoming calls to a Verasist agent via a webhook URL. Used for support lines, hotlines, and IVR replacement.

Web Calls

Web Call lets you talk to your agent directly from the browser — no phone number or telephony setup required. It runs the full pipeline: STT, LLM, TTS, recording, and transcript, exactly the same as a phone call.

Use it to try out your agent before going live. The run view shows the live transcript as the conversation progresses, node transitions as the workflow moves through the graph, and any tool or function calls the agent makes in real time.

What a run contains

After a call completes, the run record includes:

| Field | Description | |---|---| | status | Final run state | | recording_url | Download URL for the call audio | | transcript_url | Download URL for the conversation transcript | | gathered_context | Structured data extracted by the agent during the call | | initial_context | The data passed in when the call was triggered | | usage_info | Duration in seconds, token count | | cost_info | Cost in USD |

documents.title: Context & Variables
documents.excerpt: How data flows into, through, and out of a conversation
documents.content:
Verasist has a simple data model for passing information through a call. Understanding it is key to building agents that feel personalised and to extracting useful results after a call.

The three context objects

initial_context ──► Agent ──► gathered_context
                       │
                 template variables
                 (used in prompts)

initial_context

Data available to the agent before the call starts — the contact's name, account details, appointment information, anything the agent should know upfront. It can be set from several places:

  • API trigger — pass it in the request body when calling POST /public/agent/{uuid} or POST /telephony/initiate-call
  • Campaign CSV — columns beyond phone_number automatically become initial_context fields for each contact's call
  • Pre-call data fetch — enrich the context with data from your CRM or ERP via an HTTP call as the call starts, before the agent speaks
  • Agent Settings — set template context variables on the agent for testing; they're included in test calls from the workflow editor and ignored on production calls

Template variables

Values from initial_context are available in your agent's prompt using {{double_brace}} syntax.

You are calling {{customer_name}} about their {{plan}} plan,
which renews on {{renewal_date}}. Be friendly and confirm
whether they'd like to continue.

When the call starts, Verasist substitutes the values before sending the prompt to the LLM — so the agent speaks naturally as if it already knows the contact.

Fallback values

If a variable might be missing or empty, use a pipe (|) to provide a default value:

Hello {{customer_name | there}}, we're calling about your {{plan | current}} plan.

When customer_name is not set, the agent will say "Hello there" instead of leaving a blank. The syntax is:

{{variable_name | fallback_value}}

If the variable is present and non-empty, the fallback is ignored and the actual value is used.

Default variables

Built-in variables for current time and weekday, available in any prompt without setting up initial_context.

| Variable | Description | Example output | |---|---|---| | {{current_time}} | Current time in UTC (or inferred timezone) | 2026-04-02 14:30:45 UTC | | {{current_time_}} | Current time in the specified timezone | 2026-04-02 20:00:45 IST | | {{current_weekday}} | Current weekday name in UTC (or inferred timezone) | Thursday | | {{current_weekday_}} | Current weekday name in the specified timezone | Thursday |

Replace with an IANA timezone name such as Asia/Kolkata, America/New_York, or Europe/London.

Today is {{current_weekday}} and the current time is {{current_time_America/New_York}}.
When you use a timezone suffix on either current_time or current_weekday, the other variable without a suffix will automatically use the same timezone instead of UTC. For example, if your prompt contains both {{current_time_Asia/Kolkata}} and {{current_weekday}}, the weekday will also be resolved in Asia/Kolkata.

Telephony variables

For telephony calls (inbound and outbound), Verasist automatically adds these variables to initial_context:

| Variable | Description | Example | |---|---|---| | {{caller_number}} | The phone number that initiated the call | +14155550100 | | {{called_number}} | The phone number that received the call | +18005550199 |

For inbound calls, caller_number is the customer's number and called_number is your Verasist number. For outbound calls, it's the reverse — caller_number is your Verasist number and called_number is the customer's number.

You are speaking with the caller at {{caller_number}}.

gathered_context

Data the agent collects during the call. You configure what to extract in the agent node's extraction settings — each variable has a name, type, and a prompt that tells the LLM what to look for.

gathered_context is returned in the run record after the call completes and is available in webhook payloads for downstream processing. It is not available as a template variable in Agent prompts — prompts can only reference initial_context fields.

Data flow example

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Your System
    participant Dog as Verasist
    participant LLM as LLM

App->>Dog: initial_context: {customer_name: "Jane", plan: "premium"}
    Dog->>LLM: Prompt with {{customer_name}} and {{plan}} substituted
    LLM-->>Dog: Conversation response
    Note over Dog,LLM: Call progresses...
    Dog->>LLM: Extract: did the customer confirm renewal?
    LLM-->>Dog: gathered_context: {renewal_confirmed: true}
    Dog-->>App: Run record with gathered_context

Where variables are available

| Location | Variables available | |---|---| | Agent node prompts | initial_context fields via {{variable_name}} | | Edge conditions | Evaluated against the live conversation — no explicit variable syntax needed | | Webhook payload templates | All context objects via {{initial_context.field}}, {{gathered_context.field}} etc. | | Campaign CSV columns | CSV columns beyond phone_number become initial_context fields automatically |

documents.title: Campaigns
documents.excerpt: Running a voice agent against a list of contacts at scale
documents.content:
A campaign is how you run a workflow against many contacts automatically. Instead of triggering calls one by one via the API, you upload a list of phone numbers and Verasist dials them for you — respecting scheduling windows, concurrency limits, and retry rules.

How a campaign works

flowchart LR
    CSV[Contacts CSV] --> Upload[Upload to Verasist]
    Upload --> Campaign[Create Campaign]
    Campaign --> Schedule[Scheduling & Concurrency]
    Schedule --> Calls[Outbound Calls]
    Calls --> Runs[Run Records]
    Runs --> Results[Progress & Reports]
  1. Upload a contacts CSV — must have a phone_number column; any extra columns become initial_context for each call
  2. Create the campaign — link it to a workflow, set concurrency, time slots, and retry behaviour
  3. Start it — Verasist begins dialing contacts up to your concurrency limit
  4. Monitor progress — track processed, completed, failed, and pending counts in real time
  5. Pause and resume — stop and restart at any point without losing progress

The contacts CSV

The CSV drives the campaign. Each row is one contact.

phone_number,customer_name,account_id,plan
+14155550100,Jane Smith,acc_001,premium
+14155550101,Bob Jones,acc_002,basic

Columns beyond phone_number are automatically passed as initial_context to each call, making them available as template variables in your agent's prompt — so each call can feel personalised at scale.

Scheduling and concurrency

Concurrency controls how many calls run simultaneously. It's capped by your telephony plan. Set it conservatively to start.

Time slots restrict when Verasist is allowed to dial — useful for respecting business hours or regulations:

{
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "time_slots": [
    { "day": "monday", "start": "09:00", "end": "17:00" },
    { "day": "tuesday", "start": "09:00", "end": "17:00" }
  ]
}

If no time slots are set, Verasist dials continuously once the campaign is started.

Retry behaviour

Verasist can automatically retry contacts who didn't answer, were busy, or went to voicemail:

{
  "retry_config": {
    "max_attempts": 3,
    "retry_interval_minutes": 60
  }
}

Circuit breaker

The circuit breaker automatically pauses a campaign when the call failure rate gets too high — protecting against wasted spend and telephony reputation issues caused by a misconfigured agent or a bad contact list.

When enabled, Verasist monitors the failure rate within a rolling time window. If it exceeds the threshold, the campaign is paused automatically and must be manually resumed after the issue is investigated.

| Setting | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | Failure Threshold (%) | 50 | Pause when the failure rate within the window exceeds this percentage | | Window (seconds) | 120 | Rolling time window over which the failure rate is calculated | | Min Calls in Window | 5 | Minimum number of calls required before the circuit breaker can trip — prevents false positives on small samples |

A campaign paused by the circuit breaker behaves the same as a manually paused campaign — in-flight calls complete normally, and it can be resumed once the underlying issue is resolved.

Campaign lifecycle

| Status | Meaning | |---|---| | draft | Created but not started | | running | Actively dialing | | paused | Stopped; resumes from where it left off | | completed | All contacts processed | | failed | Encountered a fatal error |

You can pause and resume a campaign at any time. In-flight calls complete normally before a pause takes effect.

Results

Each contact's call creates a run record with the full transcript, recording, and gathered context — same as a manually triggered call. Use the Get Campaign Runs endpoint to retrieve them all.

See the Campaigns API reference to get started.

documents.title: Platform UI Overview
documents.excerpt: A quick reference to every organization page in the Verasist platform
documents.content:
This guide lists every user-facing page in Verasist (admin-only pages excluded), with a one-line description and the sidebar path where you'll find it.

Workflows & Agent Builder

These pages are where you create, edit, and monitor your voice agents.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Workflows Dashboard | /workflow | Lists all workflow agents organized in folders — create new workflows, upload templates, or navigate into a workflow. | | Workflow Canvas | /workflow/{id} | Drag-and-drop visual editor for building conversational agent flows with nodes and edges. | | Workflow Runs | /workflow/{id}/runs | Execution history for a specific workflow — past runs with status, duration, and cost. | | Run Detail | /workflow/{id}/run/{runId} | Full detail for a single call or chat session — transcript, context variables, audio playback, and connection logs. | | Workflow Settings | /workflow/{id}/settings | Per-workflow settings for ambient noise, template variables, dictionary, voicemail detection, recordings, and agent UUID. AI Assistant assignment is managed on the Model Configurations page, not here. | | Automation Assistant | /automation | AI chat interface with starter prompts — build, debug, test, or analyze workflows through natural language. |

Configuration

These pages manage platform-wide settings shared across workflows.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Model Configurations | /model-configurations | Choose your organization's default AI Assistant (a bundled LLM + voice + transcriber preset) and assign different Assistants to specific workflows. | | Telephony Configurations | /telephony-configurations | Manage SIP/phone configurations for inbound and outbound calling — set defaults and starred configs. | | Telephony Config Detail | /telephony-configurations/{id} | Edit a single telephony config — manage phone numbers, default caller ID, and outbound settings. | | Channels | /channels | Configure messaging channels — WhatsApp, Telegram, and Instagram. |

Tools & Integrations

Custom actions that workflows can invoke during a call.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Tools Library | /tools | Create and manage built-in tools (calculator, calendar, call history, call transfer, end call, transfer to assistant, send message) and custom tools (HTTP API, MCP). | | Tool Editor | /tools/{uuid} | Configure a single tool — HTTP method, URL, headers, parameters, and credential binding. | | API Keys | /api-keys | Create, copy, archive, and reactivate API keys for programmatic access to Verasist. |

Data & Content

Upload and manage the assets your workflows consume.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Files (Knowledge Base) | /files | Upload and manage documents for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — PDFs, text files, and more. | | Recordings | /recordings | Upload and manage audio recordings used for testing, voice samples, or pre-recorded messages. |

Outreach

Bulk outbound calling campaigns.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Campaigns Dashboard | /campaigns | List all campaigns with status badges (draft, active, paused, completed) — create new campaigns. | | New Campaign | /campaigns/new | Campaign creation wizard — select workflow, upload CSV, configure schedule, concurrency, and retries. | | Campaign Detail | /campaigns/{id} | Monitor a running campaign — start, pause, resume, redial, download reports, view call results. | | Edit Campaign | /campaigns/{id}/edit | Modify campaign name, workflow, telephony config, schedule, and advanced settings. |

Reporting & Usage

Analytics and usage tracking for your organization.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Reports | /reports | Daily call analytics — cost distribution, disposition breakdown, duration buckets, extracted variable charts. | | Usage History | /usage | Detailed table of all workflow runs with filters by date, workflow, phone number, and campaign — CSV export available. |

Organization & Account

Manage your organization profile, team, billing, and settings.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Settings | /settings | Organization and user preferences — profile, org details, MCP server config, team members, telemetry. | | Billing | /billing | Credit balance, usage charts, transaction ledger, and payment method management. | | Wallet | /wallet | Credit top-up, transaction history, and stored payment cards. | | Calendar | /calendar | Schedule and view workflow/campaign events with day, week, and month views. |

Authentication

Pre-login pages shown before entering the platform.

| Page | Path | Description | |------|------|-------------| | Login | /auth/login | Email and password sign-in (OSS/local auth mode). | | Sign Up | /auth/signup | Create a new account with name, email, phone, and organization name. | | Verify Email | /auth/verify-email | Confirms email verification after clicking the link sent post-signup — shows success/error state. |

Note: Admin-only pages (superadmin dashboard, organization management, cost configuration, etc.) are not listed here — those live under /admin and are only visible to platform administrators.

documents.title: Model Configurations
documents.excerpt: Voice Agents need AI Models to work, like LLM (Large Language Model), TTS (Voice) and STT (Transcriber). You can use any of your faviourite providers with Verasist Platform to run your Voice Agent.
documents.content:
How Model Configuration Works

Verasist bundles the AI services an agent needs — LLM, voice (TTS), transcriber (STT), and optionally a single speech-to-speech Realtime model — into a single reusable preset called an Assistant (also called a model package). Assistants are curated by your platform administrator; as an organization user, you don't pick an LLM, a voice, and a transcriber one by one — you pick an Assistant, and it brings all of those services with it.

Each Assistant card in the catalog shows the properties that matter for choosing one: cost tier, speed tier, voice gender, accent, speaking style, and language.

Verasist uses a two-level assignment system for Assistants:

  1. Organization default — the Assistant every workflow uses unless it has its own assignment.
  2. Per-workflow assignment — an optional override that points a specific workflow at a different Assistant.
If a workflow has no assignment of its own, it falls back to the organization default.
Credentials (API keys, service-account JSON, and other account-level fields) for each inference provider are managed centrally by your platform administrator, not by individual organizations — they're wired up once behind the scenes when an Assistant is created. Admins manage these credentials under Admin > Provider Credentials (/provider-credentials) and manage the Assistant catalog under Admin > Model Packages.

Choosing Your Organization's Default Assistant

To pick the Assistant your workflows use by default, go to Model Configurations in your dashboard:

  • Hosted: https://app.verasist.ai/model-configurations
  • Self-hosted: http://localhost:3010/model-configurations

  1. Under Organization Default Assistant, open the selector.
  2. Pick one of the available Assistants from the catalog — each card lists its cost tier, speed tier, voice, and language so you can compare them at a glance.
  3. Your choice is saved immediately and becomes the default for every workflow that doesn't have its own assignment.
For Verasist's own hosted models, see Service Keys for instructions on creating Service Keys.

Assigning a Different Assistant to a Specific Workflow

Different workflows often need different Assistants — for example, a customer support workflow might use a faster, cheaper Assistant, while a sales workflow uses a more capable one.

On the same Model Configurations page, under Assign Assistants to Workflows:

  1. Find the Assistant card you want to use for a specific workflow.
  2. Click Assign on that card.
  3. Select the workflow from the list.
  4. Confirm — that workflow now uses this Assistant instead of the organization default.
To revert a workflow back to the organization default, remove its assignment from the same list.
Assistant selection and assignment both happen on the Model Configurations page — not inside an individual workflow's Settings tab. An Assistant built on a Realtime provider (like Gemini Live) works the same way: pick it as the organization default or assign it to a workflow, and that workflow uses the bundled speech-to-speech model instead of separate TTS/STT services. An LLM is still bundled alongside the Realtime model for out-of-band tasks like variable extraction and QA analysis, which the realtime service does not handle. Context compaction is not applicable in Realtime mode.

Gemini 3.1 Live

Gemini 3.1 Live is Google's realtime multimodal API that handles both LLM and voice in a single model. Instead of configuring separate LLM, TTS, and STT services, Gemini Live acts as an all-in-one realtime provider — it processes speech input, generates a response, and speaks it back, all over a single streaming connection.

Verasist supports Gemini 3.1 Live as a Realtime provider. The default model is gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview.

Available Voices

You can choose from the following built-in voices:

| Voice | Description | |-------|-------------| | Puck | Default voice | | Charon | — | | Kore | — | | Fenrir | — | | Aoede | — |

Getting a Gemini API Key (admin setup)

A Gemini API key must be configured once by a platform administrator before any organization can use google_realtime. Follow these steps:

  1. Go to Google AI Studio.
  2. Sign in with your Google account.
  3. Click on Get API Key in the left sidebar.
  4. Click Create API Key.
  5. Select an existing Google Cloud project or create a new one.
  6. Copy the generated API key and store it securely.
  7. As a supervisor/admin, go to Admin > Provider Credentials (/provider-credentials), open the Realtime tab, select google_realtime, and paste the API key.
The Gemini API key is different from a Google Cloud service account key. You specifically need a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio for use with Verasist.

Selecting an Assistant that uses Gemini 3.1 Live

Once an admin has configured the google_realtime credential and published an Assistant built on it (model gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview, a voice such as Puck, and a language):

  1. Go to Model Configurations in your Verasist dashboard (https://app.verasist.ai/model-configurations for hosted or http://localhost:3010/model-configurations for local).
  2. Pick that Assistant as your Organization Default, or Assign it to the specific workflow(s) that should use Gemini 3.1 Live.
You don't select the provider, model, or voice yourself, and you don't need an API key — those are already set on the Assistant by whoever created it.
When using a Realtime provider like Gemini Live, you do not need to configure separate TTS and STT services — the realtime model handles speech in and out. However, you must still configure an LLM under the LLM tab: it powers variable extraction and QA analysis, which the realtime service does not perform.

Gemini Live on Vertex AI

If you want to run Gemini Live through your own Google Cloud project — for billing consolidation, VPC controls, regional residency, or enterprise IAM — Verasist also supports Gemini Live via Vertex AI as a separate provider (google_vertex_realtime). The default model is google/gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio.

Unlike Google AI Studio (which uses a single Gemini API key), Vertex AI authenticates with a service account belonging to your Google Cloud project.

Prerequisites (admin setup)

These steps are performed once by a platform administrator, not by individual organizations.

  1. A Google Cloud project with billing enabled.
  2. The Vertex AI API enabled on that project:
   gcloud services enable aiplatform.googleapis.com --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID
  1. A service account with the Vertex AI User role (roles/aiplatform.user) on the project:
   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
     --member="serviceAccount:YOUR_SA@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
     --role="roles/aiplatform.user"
  1. A JSON key for that service account (P12 keys are not supported).

Creating the service account key

  1. In the GCP Console, go to IAM & Admin → Service Accounts.
  2. Pick an existing service account (or create a new one).
  3. Open the Keys tab → Add Key → Create new key.
  4. Choose JSON as the key type and click Create.
  5. The key file will download to your computer — store it securely and treat it as a secret.
Always pick JSON, not P12. The Vertex AI client libraries used by Verasist only accept service-account JSON keys; P12 is a legacy format retained for older Google Workspace integrations.

Configuring Vertex AI Realtime (admin setup)

  1. As a supervisor/admin, go to Admin > Provider Credentials (/provider-credentials).
  2. Open the Realtime tab and select google_vertex_realtime.
  3. Fill in the account-level fields:
| Field | What to put in | |---|---| | Project Id | The project_id value from your service-account JSON | | Location | GCP region where the model is available (e.g. us-east4) | | Credentials | Paste the entire contents of the service-account JSON file |
  1. Save the credential.
Paste the whole JSON file into the Credentials field — including private_key, client_email, and all other entries. Don't try to extract individual fields. If Credentials is left blank, Verasist falls back to Application Default Credentials (ADC) from the host environment, which is useful when running Verasist on a GCP VM or GKE pod with an attached service account.
IAM changes can take up to ~60 seconds to propagate. If you see Permission 'aiplatform.endpoints.predict' denied, wait a minute and retry — or double-check that the role was granted to the same service account whose JSON you pasted.

Selecting an Assistant that uses Vertex AI Realtime

Once an admin has configured the google_vertex_realtime credential and published an Assistant built on it (model, voice, and language already set):

  1. Go to Model Configurations in your Verasist dashboard.
  2. Pick that Assistant as your Organization Default, or Assign it to the specific workflow(s) that should use it.
No provider, model, or account fields are shown to you — they're already baked into the Assistant.

documents.title: LLM
documents.excerpt: Configure the Large Language Model that powers your voice agent's ability to understand context and generate conversational responses.
documents.content:
Your voice agent's intelligence comes from its LLM (Large Language Model). The LLM processes the caller's transcribed speech, understands the conversation context, and decides what to say next — including when to invoke tools or transition between nodes.

As an organization user, you don't pick an LLM provider/model directly for a workflow — you pick a pre-built Assistant that already bundles an LLM, voice, and transcriber. This page describes what LLM providers are available inside an Assistant. See Model Configurations for how Assistants are selected and assigned.

Supported Providers

Verasist supports the following LLM providers out of the box:

| Provider | Best For | |----------|----------| | OpenAI | General purpose, strong reasoning (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini) | | Anthropic | Nuanced conversations, safety-critical use cases (Claude) | | Google | Multilingual support, Gemini family | | Groq | Ultra-low latency inference | | Azure | Enterprise compliance, private deployment | | DeepSeek | Cost-efficient reasoning | | Together / Fireworks | Open-source model access |

Adding a Custom Model

If you don't find your preferred model in the dropdown, you can add it manually by entering the model ID as recognized by the provider's API.

Model Recommendations

For Voice Agents

Voice conversations require fast responses. Choose models optimized for low latency:
  • OpenAI: gpt-4o-mini for most use cases, gpt-4o for complex reasoning
  • Anthropic: claude-3-haiku for speed, claude-3.5-sonnet for quality
  • Groq: llama-3.1-70b or mixtral-8x7b for fastest responses

For Extraction & QA

Post-call extraction and QA analysis can use more powerful models since latency is not a concern:
  • gpt-4o, claude-3.5-sonnet, or gemini-1.5-pro

Global vs. Agent-Level Configuration

You don't pick an LLM directly. Verasist bundles the LLM together with a voice and a transcriber into a reusable Assistant (model package), curated by your platform administrator:

  • Organization Default: The Assistant used when a workflow has no assignment of its own. Chosen under Model Configurations.
  • Per-Workflow Assignment: Any workflow can be assigned a different Assistant — and therefore a different LLM — from the same Model Configurations page.
See Model Configurations for the full Assistant selection and assignment flow.

documents.title: Voice
documents.excerpt: Configure the Text-to-Speech engine and voice that your AI agent uses to speak to callers.
documents.content:
The TTS (Text-to-Speech) engine converts the LLM's text responses into spoken audio. The voice you choose defines how your agent sounds to callers — its accent, tone, pacing, and language.

As an organization user, you don't pick a TTS provider/voice directly for a workflow — you pick a pre-built Assistant that already bundles a voice, LLM, and transcriber. This page describes what voice providers are available inside an Assistant. See Model Configurations for how Assistants are selected and assigned.

Supported Providers

| Provider | Best For | |----------|----------| | ElevenLabs | Most natural voices, voice cloning, multilingual | | OpenAI | Consistent quality, simple setup | | Deepgram | Low latency, Aura voices | | Azure | Enterprise compliance, neural voices | | PlayHT | Conversational voices, emotion control | | Cartesia | Ultra-low latency, streaming TTS | | Rime | Expressive, context-aware speech |

Selecting a Voice

  1. Choose a provider from the dropdown
  2. Select a voice from the pre-loaded list, or
  3. Enter a custom voice ID manually from the provider's documentation

Voice Selection Tips

  • Match your brand: A warm, friendly voice for customer service; a professional tone for B2B
  • Language matters: Ensure the voice supports your callers' primary language with native accent
  • Test with your script: Read your agent's typical responses aloud — does the voice feel natural?
  • Consider latency: Some providers stream audio faster than others; test with real calls

Global vs. Agent-Level Configuration

You don't pick a voice directly. Verasist bundles the TTS voice together with an LLM and a transcriber into a reusable Assistant (model package), curated by your platform administrator:

  • Organization Default: The Assistant used when a workflow has no assignment of its own.
  • Agent Override: Any workflow can be assigned a different Assistant — and therefore a different voice — from the Model Configurations page.
See Model Configurations for setup instructions.

documents.title: Transcriber
documents.excerpt: Configure the Speech-to-Text engine that converts caller speech into text for your AI agent to understand and respond to.
documents.content:
The STT (Speech-to-Text) engine converts the caller's spoken words into text that the LLM can process. Transcription quality directly impacts your agent's understanding — errors at this stage cascade through the entire conversation.

As an organization user, you don't pick an STT provider directly for a workflow — you pick a pre-built Assistant that already bundles a transcriber, LLM, and voice. This page describes what transcriber providers are available inside an Assistant. See Model Configurations for how Assistants are selected and assigned.

Supported Providers

| Provider | Best For | |----------|----------| | Deepgram | Low latency, Nova-3 model, broad language support | | OpenAI | Whisper models, strong accuracy | | Azure | Enterprise compliance, custom speech models | | AssemblyAI | Advanced features (entity detection, sentiment) | | Groq | Fast Whisper inference | | Gladia | Real-time transcription, speaker diarization | | Cartesia | Streaming STT with low latency |

Language Configuration

Selecting the right language model is critical for accuracy:

  • Match the caller's language: Most providers have language-specific models (e.g., Deepgram's nova-3 supports 30+ languages)
  • Multi-language calls: Some models auto-detect language; others require pre-selection
  • Accents & dialects: Test with real voice samples from your target audience
Example: Deepgram language support at developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview#nova-3

Model Selection Tips

  • For English calls: nova-3 (Deepgram) or whisper-1 (OpenAI) provide excellent accuracy
  • For multilingual calls: Choose a model with auto-detection to handle code-switching
  • For noisy environments: Look for models with noise reduction (Deepgram's Nova-3 includes this)
  • For real-time: Streaming models from Deepgram, Cartesia, or Gladia minimize end-to-end latency

Global vs. Agent-Level Configuration

You don't pick a transcriber directly. Verasist bundles the STT transcriber together with an LLM and a voice into a reusable Assistant (model package), curated by your platform administrator:

  • Organization Default: The Assistant used when a workflow has no assignment of its own.
  • Agent Override: Any workflow can be assigned a different Assistant — and therefore a different transcriber (e.g., a different language) — from the Model Configurations page.
See Model Configurations for setup instructions.

documents.title: API Keys and Service Keys
documents.excerpt: You can create API Keys to trigger Verasist Voice Agents and Service Keys to use with Inference Providers
documents.content:
The option to create the Keys are in https://app.verasist.ai/api-keys if you are using hosted version, or http://localhost:3010/api-keys if you are using the self hosted version.

API Keys

API keys can be used to trigger a voice agent from an external system, like n8n or programatically from your other workflows. In order to generate that, you can go to /api-keys and create a new key.

Please note that you must copy and keep the API key secretly, since this is the only time that you would be able to copy it. If you lose it, you can always delete that, if its not being used anywhere, and create a new API key.

Service Keys

Service Keys are the keys which you generate to be used in Model Configurations. In order to generate that, you can go to /api-keys and create a new key.

documents.title: Agent UUID
documents.excerpt: Find and use your workflow's stable Agent UUID
documents.content:
The Agent UUID is the workflow's stable identifier. In API routes and payloads you may also see it called workflow_uuid.

Unlike numeric workflow IDs, the Agent UUID is portable across environments and does not change when you publish new versions of the same workflow.

Where to find it

You can copy the Agent UUID from two places in the dashboard.

From the workflow editor

  1. Open your agent in the workflow editor
  2. Click the ⋮ menu in the top-right of the header
  3. Click Copy Agent UUID

From the agent's Settings page

  1. Open the agent and go to Settings
  2. Scroll to the Agent UUID section
  3. Click the UUID code block, or use Copy UUID

Where you use it

Use the Agent UUID for workflow-level routes such as:

  • POST /api/v1/public/agent/workflow/{workflow_uuid}
  • POST /api/v1/public/agent/test/workflow/{workflow_uuid}
  • wss:///api/v1/agent-stream/{agent_uuid}
Do not confuse the Agent UUID with an API Trigger node UUID (trigger_path).
  • Use the Agent UUID for workflow-level routes like /public/agent/workflow/{workflow_uuid}
  • Use the API Trigger node UUID for trigger routes like /public/agent/{uuid}
  • The API Trigger node path can be edited if you want something more descriptive
  • The Agent UUID is generated by Verasist and cannot be changed
See API Trigger for trigger-node URLs.

documents.title: Interruption Handling
documents.excerpt: Control whether users can interrupt the bot while it is speaking by configuring the Allow Interruption toggle on each node.
documents.content:
Overview

Interruption handling controls whether the user can "barge in" and interrupt the bot while it is speaking. This is configured per node in the workflow editor, giving you fine-grained control over conversation flow.

How It Works

Each node in your workflow has an Allow Interruption toggle:

  • Disabled (default) — The bot finishes its entire response before accepting user input. The user's microphone is temporarily muted while the bot speaks.
  • Enabled — The bot stops speaking as soon as the user starts talking, and immediately processes their input. This creates a natural, conversational experience.
When interruption is disabled and the user tries to speak during bot speech, a one-time warning appears in the live transcript indicating that interruption is disabled for that step.

When to Disable Interruption

Disabling interruption is useful when the bot needs to deliver a complete message without being cut off:

  • Legal disclaimers — Ensure the full disclaimer is spoken before proceeding.
  • Critical instructions — Step-by-step directions that lose meaning if partially heard.
  • Greeting or introduction — Let the bot finish its opening before the user responds.
  • Confirmation summaries — Read back important details (appointment times, order totals) in full.

When to Enable Interruption

Keep interruption enabled for interactive conversation stages:

  • Q&A or objection handling — Let the user jump in naturally.
  • Open-ended discussion — Feels more human when either party can interject.
  • Long responses — Allow the user to redirect if the bot goes off track.

Configuring Interruption

  1. Open your workflow in the Voice Agent Builder.
  2. Select the node you want to configure.
  3. Toggle Allow Interruption on or off in the node settings panel.
  4. Save your workflow.
You can set different interruption behavior for each node. For example, disable interruption on your Start Node greeting but enable it on all subsequent Agent Nodes.

What the User Experiences

| Interruption | Bot Speaking | User Speaks | Result | |---|---|---|---| | Enabled | Yes | Yes | Bot stops, processes user input | | Disabled | Yes | Yes | Bot continues, user input is ignored until bot finishes | | Either | No | Yes | User input is processed normally |

When interruption is disabled, the platform mutes the user's audio input while the bot is speaking. Once the bot finishes, the microphone is automatically unmuted and the user can respond normally.

documents.title: Tracing
documents.excerpt: Trace your agent runs to debug issues, understand LLM behavior, and refine your prompts.
documents.content:
Overview

Tracing gives you full visibility into what happened during a test call or live call. It's one of the most powerful features for making your voice agents production-ready.

With traces, you can see:

  • The exact conversation that occurred
  • What prompts were sent to the LLM
  • Which tools the LLM had access to (and which it called)
  • Speech-to-text transcriptions of user input and Transcription errors
  • Tool call requests and responses

Accessing Traces

After a call ends, you'll see a call summary screen. Click the Traces tab to view the detailed trace log for that call.

Understanding Trace Sections

Traces are organized by event type. The two most important sections to focus on are:

STT (Speech-to-Text)

These entries capture the transcription of what the user said during the call. Each STT entry shows the text conversion of the user's speech at that point in the conversation.

Example:

STT: "Yeah, I would want to check what your operating hours are."

LLM (Language Model Calls)

These entries show every call made to the LLM. Each LLM trace includes:

  • Prompt - The full prompt sent to the LLM (combination of global prompt + node-specific prompt)
  • Conversation history - The entire conversation up to that point
  • Available tools - All tools the LLM can access for that node
  • Response - What the LLM generated

Tools in Traces

Each LLM call shows the tools available to the agent at that moment. These fall into three categories:

System Tools (Default)

Every node includes these by default:

  • Safe Calculator — Helps LLMs perform math accurately
  • Get Current Time — Retrieves current time
  • Convert Time — Converts time to a specific timezone

Pathway Tools

These correspond to the pathways (node transitions) you've configured. For example, if your node has pathways to "End Call" and "Move to Summary," you'll see those as available tools.

The tool descriptions shown in traces match the descriptions you set in your pathway configuration.

Custom Tools

Any external tools you've attached to the node (e.g. any custom tools you created for API endpoints for booking, order submission, etc.) will appear here. See the custom tools documentation.

Tool Calls in Traces

When the LLM decides to call a tool, you'll see:

  1. Tool call request — The tool name and parameters sent
  2. Tool response — The result returned (e.g., {"status": "ok"})
The tool call and response also appear in subsequent conversation history, so the LLM knows the outcome.

Example flow:

User: "Can you book me a table for tomorrow at 7pm?"

LLM calls: book_table(date: "tomorrow", time: "7pm", party_size: 2)

Tool response: ``{"status": "done", "confirmation": "Table booked"}`

Agent: "I've booked your table for tomorrow at 7pm."

How Prompts Are Combined

The prompt sent to the LLM is a combination of:

  1. Global Prompt — Defined in your Global Node settings
  2. Node Prompt — Defined in the specific node being executed
If you disable the Global Node for a particular node, only the node-specific prompt will be used.

Key Concept: Conversation History

Every time an LLM call is made, the entire conversation history up to that point is passed to the LLM. This means:

  • The LLM always has full context
  • You can see exactly what context the LLM had when it made a decision
  • Useful for debugging unexpected responses

Setting Up Langfuse Tracing

We provide seamless integration with Langfuse for tracing if you want to use your own account. This enables you to use the playground feature of Langfuse. This works on both managed and self-hosted Verasist deployments.

Setup steps:

  1. Sign up at Langfuse and create API credentials
  2. In the Verasist UI, go to Platform Settings (/settings) and enter your Langfuse host, public key, and secret key
  3. Click Save
Once enabled, traces will be available for every completed call in Verasist.
For self-hosted deployments, you can also configure Langfuse via environment variables (LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY, LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY, LANGFUSE_HOST`) as a default for all organizations. Tracing activates automatically once credentials are available — no separate enable flag is required. Per-organization credentials set in the UI take precedence over environment variables.

Quick Reference

| Trace Type | What It Shows | |------------|---------------| | STT | User speech transcribed to text | | LLM | Prompt + conversation + tools + response | | Tool Call | Tool invocation and response |

Tips for Using Traces

  • Debug unexpected responses — Check the LLM trace to see what prompt and context the model received
  • Verify tool calls — Confirm tools are being triggered with correct parameters
  • Refine prompts — Use traces to see how your prompt instructions affect LLM behavior
  • Check transcription accuracy — Review STT entries if the agent misunderstands users

documents.title: Voice Agent Builder
documents.excerpt: Verasist provides UI components to build a voice Agent. The voice agent can be created by going to https://app.verasist.ai/workflow and then Creating a new Agent.
documents.content:
We provide an Agent which quickly helps you get started by creating a voice agent with default prompts and pathways. You can provide inputs like whether you need an "Inbound" or "Outbound" voice agent. You can also provide your use case, and description of what the voice agent should be doing. Your inputs will be sent to an LLM to generate the voice agent, so the better you can describe your use case, the better the starting agent will be created for you.

Once you create your Voice Agent using our Agent builder, you would be taken to the Agent, where you would have an option to test the agent using "Web Call" or "Phone Call". You can also modify the prompts of the Agent to suit it to your use case better.

documents.title: Editing a Workflow
documents.excerpt: Learn the fundamentals of building workflows with nodes, pathways, and conversation flow in the voice agent builder.
documents.content:
Overview

A workflow is a graph of connected nodes representing conversation stages, with pathways defining agent movement between stages.

Global Node

Contains instructions applicable across the entire call:

  • Company context
  • Overall agent goal
  • Tone and personality
  • Common objection handling

Node-Level Toggles

Add Global Prompt

  • Recommended to inject Global Node instructions into most nodes

Allow Interruption

  • Default "On": Bot stops and responds to user interruption
  • "Off": Bot continues speaking, ignoring user input

Detect Voicemail

  • Available only in Start Node
  • Automatically disconnects if voicemail detected

Variable Extraction

Supported in Agent and End Call Nodes:

  • Extract structured variables
  • Define name, type, and description
  • Examples: customer name, budget, interest

Webhook Node

  • Executed at call end
  • Sends payload to specific endpoint
  • Use for:
- Storing call data - Triggering automation - Syncing with CRMs

Editing Workflows

  • Selectively delete nodes/pathways
  • Completely reset workflow

Pathways and Tool Calls

  • Define agent node movement
  • Use tool calls to transition between nodes
  • "tool" is a reserved keyword for function calls and actions

documents.title: Pre-recorded Audio
documents.excerpt: Build hybrid voice agents that combine pre-recorded audio with dynamic text generation for lower latency, reduced TTS costs, and natural-sounding conversations.
documents.content:
Custom recordings allow you to build hybrid voice agents that use your own pre-recorded audio for key parts of the conversation, while falling back to LLM-generated speech (via a cloned voice) for dynamic responses. This gives you the best of both worlds — the emotional depth of real human speech and the flexibility of AI-generated dialogue.

Why use custom recordings?

  • Reduced TTS cost — Pre-recorded audio is played directly, so you are not charged for TTS synthesis on those segments.
  • Emotional variance — Real recordings carry natural intonation and emotion that TTS cannot fully replicate.
  • Lower latency — Playing a pre-recorded clip is faster than synthesizing text at runtime.

Prerequisites

  • A TTS provider that supports voice cloning (e.g., Cartesia, ElevenLabs, or Deepgram).
  • An API key for your chosen TTS provider, configured in Voice settings.

Step 1: Clone your voice

Clone your voice with your TTS provider so that dynamically generated speech sounds similar to your recordings. For example, with Cartesia:

  1. Go to Cartesia and navigate to Instant Clone.
  2. Record a short audio clip (up to 10 seconds) of your voice.
  3. Give the clone a name and select your language.
  4. Copy the Voice ID — you will need it in the next step.
You can use any TTS provider that supports voice cloning. The steps will vary by provider, but the key output is always a Voice ID tied to your cloned voice.

Step 2: Configure the cloned voice in Verasist

  1. Go to your agent's Model Configuration in the Verasist dashboard.
  2. Under voice settings, select Add Voice ID manually.
  3. Paste the Voice ID from your cloned voice.
  4. Make sure the provider matches where you cloned your voice (e.g., Cartesia).
  5. Enter the provider's API key if you haven't already.
  6. Save the configuration.

Step 3: Upload recordings

Navigate to the Recordings page in the Verasist dashboard. Recordings are shared across all agents in your organization. You can either upload pre-recorded audio files or record directly in the browser.

For each recording:

  1. Click Upload Recording.
  2. Choose an audio file or click Record to record in the browser.
  3. Verify the transcription is correct — edit it if needed.
  4. Click Upload.
You can rename a recording's ID at any time by clicking the edit icon next to it in the recordings list.

Step 4: Build the workflow

Open your agent's workflow and write the conversation flow in natural language. To insert a recording, type @ in the prompt editor — this will show a list of all available recordings in your organization.

For any user question that falls outside your recordings, the agent automatically generates a dynamic response using the LLM, which is then synthesized using your cloned voice via TTS.

Tips for best results

  • Record in a quiet environment to improve audio quality and consistency with the cloned voice.
  • Use pro cloning services (when available) and provide more sample audio for a higher-quality voice clone.
  • Keep recordings concise — short, focused clips work best for specific conversation moments.
  • Review call recordings after testing to identify where the transition between pre-recorded and dynamic audio can be improved.

documents.title: Template Variables
documents.excerpt: You can use Template Variables in your prompts for your Agent nodes, or when constructing the payload for the Webhook Node
documents.content:
Template Rendering

You reference template variables with {{double_brace}} syntax. The data comes from initial_context — set via the API Trigger, a campaign sheet, or a Pre-Call Data Fetch that enriches the context when the call starts — and, in Webhook payloads only, from gathered_context (variables extracted during the call).

The syntax depends on where you use it:

| Where | initial_context | gathered_context | | --- | --- | --- | | Agent node prompts | {{field_name}} (referenced directly) | Not available | | Webhook Node payloads | {{initial_context.field_name}} | {{gathered_context.field_name}} |

Agent node prompts

In an Agent node prompt, reference each initial_context field directly by name. Nested values are supported with dot notation.

Example: if the initial context is

{
    "initial_context": {
        "user": {
            "name": "John"
        }
    }
}

write your prompt to access the user's name as below:

Prompt: You are Alice, who is talking to {{user.name}}.

Variables extracted during the call (gathered_context) are not available in Agent prompts — a prompt can only reference initial_context fields. To act on extracted data, send it to a Webhook Node.

Webhook Node payloads

When constructing a Webhook Node payload, the context objects are nested under their names, so reference them with the initial_context. and gathered_context. prefixes:

Payload value: {{initial_context.user.name}} or {{gathered_context.call_disposition}}

Using Template Variables for Testing

Template variables defined in your workflow Settings > Context Variables are included in test calls (both web and phone) made from the workflow editor. This is useful for simulating data that would normally come from telephony or an API trigger.

For example, you can set caller_number and called_number as context variables to test Pre-Call Data Fetch without needing a real inbound call.

These context variables are only used during test calls from the workflow editor. On production inbound calls and campaign outbound calls, the actual telephony data is used and these values are ignored.

Nodes

Verasist Voice Agents are composed of various nodes. These nodes can provide instructions to the voice agent, help you setup a trigger where you can trigger the voice agent to call someone, or help you setup a webhook, where you can update the results of the call in your CRM or trigger a downstream workflow in n8n. In the next steps, we will be documenting the nodes that you can use in building the voice agent.

documents.title: Pre-Call Data Fetch
documents.excerpt: Fetch customer data from your CRM or ERP before the call starts, so your voice agent can greet callers by name and reference their account details.
documents.content:
Pre-Call Data Fetch allows you to enrich the call context with external data before the voice agent starts speaking. When enabled on the Start Call node, Verasist sends an HTTP request to your API as soon as a call is initiated. While the response is loading, the caller hears a ring-back tone. Once the data arrives, it is merged into the call's initial context and becomes available as template variables in your prompts and greetings.

How It Works

  1. A call arrives (inbound) or is initiated (outbound).
  2. Verasist sends a POST request to your configured endpoint with a standardized payload.
  3. The caller hears a ring-back tone while waiting for the response.
  4. Your API responds with a JSON object containing an initial_context object.
  5. The variables are merged into the call's initial context.
  6. The voice agent starts with full access to the fetched data via {{variable_name}} syntax.

Configuration

Open the Start Call node editor and expand Advanced Settings. Toggle Pre-Call Data Fetch and configure:

| Field | Description | | --- | --- | | Endpoint URL | The URL Verasist will send the POST request to. | | Authentication | Optional credential for authenticating the request. Supports API key, bearer token, basic auth, and custom header. |

Request Format

Verasist sends a POST request with the following JSON payload:

{
  "event": "call_inbound",
  "call_inbound": {
    "agent_id": 123,
    "from_number": "+12137771234",
    "to_number": "+12137771235"
  }
}

| Field | Description | | --- | --- | | event | Always "call_inbound". | | call_inbound.agent_id | The workflow (agent) ID. | | call_inbound.from_number | The caller's phone number (caller_number from initial context). | | call_inbound.to_number | The called phone number (called_number from initial context). |

The Content-Type header is set to application/json. If you configured a credential, the corresponding authentication header is included.

Expected Response Format

Your API should return a JSON object with a 2xx status code. The variables to inject into the call context should be placed inside the initial_context key:

{
  "call_inbound": {
    "initial_context": {
      "customer_name": "Jane Doe",
      "account_status": "active",
      "loyalty_tier": "gold",
      "open_tickets": 2
    }
  }
}

You can also place initial_context at the top level:

{
  "initial_context": {
    "customer_name": "Jane Doe",
    "account_status": "active"
  }
}
The legacy dynamic_variables key is still accepted as a drop-in alias for initial_context, so existing integrations keep working without any changes. Use initial_context for new integrations. If a response contains both keys, initial_context takes precedence.

After the response is received, you can reference these values anywhere template variables are supported:

  • Greeting: Hello {{customer_name}}, thank you for calling!
  • Prompt: The customer is a {{loyalty_tier}} member with {{open_tickets}} open support tickets.
If the response is not a valid JSON object, does not contain initial_context (or the legacy dynamic_variables), or the request fails or times out, the call proceeds normally without the additional context. The pre-call fetch never blocks or fails a call.

Nested Variables

If your initial_context contains nested objects, you can access them using dot notation:

{
  "call_inbound": {
    "initial_context": {
      "customer": {
        "name": "Jane Doe",
        "address": {
          "city": "Los Angeles"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Access in prompts as {{customer.name}} and {{customer.address.city}}.

Timeout

The request has a 10-second timeout. If your API does not respond within this window, the call proceeds without the fetched data. Design your endpoint to respond as quickly as possible to minimize the ring-back tone duration.

Testing with Test Calls

documents.title: Tools
documents.excerpt: Extend your voice agent's capabilities by giving it tools to perform actions during live conversations.
documents.content:
Tools let your AI agent take actions during a conversation — transfer calls, end calls, call external APIs, or invoke remote MCP servers — based on the context of the conversation and your prompt instructions.

When a tool is attached to a workflow node, the LLM decides when to invoke it and what parameters to pass, based on the user's spoken intent and your node-level instructions.

Tool Types

Verasist provides two categories of tools:

Built-in Tools

Pre-configured tools that handle common telephony operations out of the box:

  • Call Transfer — Transfer the active call to a phone number or SIP endpoint
  • End Call — Terminate the call when the conversation is complete
  • Calculator — Perform safe arithmetic calculations during calls
  • Calendar — Create appointments, reminders, notes, and todos during calls
  • Transfer to Assistant — Hand off the conversation to another workflow or assistant
  • Transfer to Channel — Move a live call or chat to a new conversation on WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram, carrying over the history
  • Call History — Search past interactions across all channels for caller context
  • Incoming Messages — Search inbound WhatsApp, Telegram, and Instagram messages received through your connected channels
  • Send Message — Send a WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram message through a configured chat channel during a call

Integrations

Tools that act through a third-party account you connect under Settings:

  • CRM — Search, create, update, and list contacts in a connected HubSpot or Microsoft Dynamics 365 account
  • Email — Send and search email through a connected Gmail or Microsoft mailbox
  • Google Calendar — Create, check, update, and cancel events on a connected Google Calendar
  • Google Sheets — Append, read, and update rows in a connected Google Sheet
  • Google Tasks — Create, list, and complete tasks in a connected Google Tasks account
  • Trendyol — Answer customer questions and check order/claim status on a connected Trendyol seller account
  • Yemek Sepeti — Look up, update, and list orders on a connected Yemek Sepeti partner account

Custom Tools

Tools you define to integrate with any external system:

  • HTTP API — Call any REST API endpoint during a conversation (e.g., CRM updates, data lookups, triggering automations)
  • MCP Tool — Connect an external MCP server and expose its remote tools to the LLM during a conversation
  • Web Page Query — Fetch public web pages and read their clean text content during a conversation

How Tools Work

  1. You define a tool with a name, description, and parameters
  2. You attach the tool to one or more workflow nodes
  3. During a call, the LLM reads your node prompt, the tool description, and the caller's intent to decide whether to invoke the tool
  4. The tool executes and returns a result that the agent can use to continue the conversation

Creating Tools via the Automation Assistant

Instead of creating a tool by hand under Tools, you can ask the Automation Assistant (the chat assistant on the Automation page) to do it for you conversationally — e.g. "add an HTTP tool that looks up order status." The assistant first checks your existing tools and reuses a matching one if it finds one, so you don't end up with duplicates; it only creates a new tool when nothing fits. Once created (or reused), it attaches the tool's UUID to the relevant node(s) in the agent it's building or editing for you.

Best Practices

  • Attach only relevant tools to each node — fewer tools means more reliable invocations
  • Write clear tool descriptions — the LLM uses these to decide when to call the tool
  • Guide the LLM in your node prompt — explicitly describe when a tool should be used
  • Test tool behavior — verify your agent invokes tools at the right moments using web or phone calls

documents.title: Calculator
documents.excerpt: Allow your AI agent to perform safe arithmetic calculations during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Calculator tool enables your AI agent to evaluate arithmetic expressions during calls. It uses a safe AST-based evaluator that only permits basic math operations — no arbitrary code execution.

How It Works

The Calculator tool exposes a single safe_calculator function to the LLM:

  1. Agent Decision: The agent encounters a math problem during conversation (e.g., pricing calculation, date math, totals)
  2. Expression Evaluation: The expression is parsed through Python's AST and only allowed node types (+, -, , /, *, %, parentheses) are permitted
  3. Result Returned: The numeric result is returned to the agent, which can incorporate it into the conversation

Supported Operations

| Operator | Description | Example | |----------|-------------|---------| | + | Addition | 2000 + 500 | | - | Subtraction | 1000 - 350 | | | Multiplication | 150 3 | | / | Division | 1200 / 4 | | | Exponentiation | 2 10 | | % | Modulo (remainder) | 17 % 5 | | () | Parentheses (grouping) | (100 + 50) * 2 |

Configuration

The Calculator tool has no additional configuration — it's ready to use out of the box. Simply add it to your workflow node from the Tools panel.

Agent Usage

Your AI agent calls the calculator with an arithmetic expression:

safe_calculator(expression="(150 * 3) + (75 / 5)")

Common scenarios:

  • Calculating totals, discounts, or tax during sales calls
  • Date and time arithmetic (e.g., "What date is 45 days from now?")
  • Unit conversions (e.g., square footage, currency with fixed rates)
  • Splitting bills or calculating per-person costs
  • Any math the caller asks about during the conversation
The calculator only supports numeric arithmetic. It cannot access external APIs, databases, or execute arbitrary code. For complex calculations that depend on external data, use an HTTP API tool instead.

documents.title: Calendar
documents.excerpt: Allow your AI agent to create and query calendar entries such as appointments, reminders, notes, and todos during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Calendar tool enables your AI agent to manage calendar entries — create new appointments, notes, reminders, or todos, and search existing entries — all during a live conversation.

How It Works

The Calendar tool exposes two functions to the LLM:

  1. Write (Create Entry): The agent creates a new calendar entry with a date, optional time, title, and description
  2. Read (Query Entries): The agent searches existing entries by date range or keyword
When a caller asks "Do I have anything scheduled next week?" or "Can you set a reminder for my dentist appointment?", the agent uses the Calendar tool to read or write entries.

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Entry Type: The default type of entry this tool creates. Choose one of:
- note — General note - appointment — Scheduled appointment - reminder — Time-based reminder - todo — Task to be completed
  • Default Title Template: Optional template for auto-generating entry titles using {{initial_context.}} and {{gathered_context.}} variables
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes

Agent Usage

Creating an Entry

Your AI agent creates calendar entries with date, title, and optional time/description:

calendar_tool(date="2026-07-10", time="14:00", title="Dentist Appointment", description="Annual checkup at Dr. Smith's office")

Querying Entries

The agent can search existing entries by date range or keyword:

calendar_tool_read(start_date="2026-07-01", end_date="2026-07-31", query="dentist")

Common scenarios:

  • Caller asks to schedule an appointment or set a reminder
  • Caller asks what appointments they have coming up
  • Agent needs to check availability before booking
  • Recording meeting notes during the call

Entry Types

| Type | Description | |------|-------------| | note | A general note without specific time constraints | | appointment | A scheduled meeting or appointment with a date/time | | reminder | A time-based reminder for future action | | todo | A task item to be completed | | trigger | A scheduled action (see Scheduled Triggers below) — created automatically when action_type is set |

The agent automatically uses the configured default entry type, but can suggest a different type based on conversation context.

Scheduled Triggers

Beyond plain notes and reminders, a calendar entry can also be a scheduled trigger that automatically kicks off a workflow run or controls a call campaign at a future date/time — with optional recurrence. Triggers are checked and executed automatically roughly once a minute.

Both your AI agent (via the Calendar tool) and you (from the Calendar page in the dashboard) can create, edit, and delete these triggers.

Trigger Actions

| action_type | Effect | |---|---| | workflow_run | Starts a new run of the specified workflow | | campaign_start | Starts the specified call campaign | | campaign_pause | Pauses the specified call campaign |

For workflow_run triggers, you also choose:

  • mode — the run mode, e.g. textchat or webrtc (used when action_channel is text, the default)
  • action_channel — how the workflow is launched: text (default, no external channel), phone, whatsapp, telegram, or instagram
- phone requires an action_target phone number and dials out through your organization's default (or a specifically chosen) telephony configuration - whatsapp/telegram/instagram require an action_target (phone/JID or chat ID) and a action_channel_configuration_id picking which saved channel credential to use

Recurrence

Set recurrence to make a trigger repeat instead of firing once:

{"frequency": "weekly", "interval": 1, "days_of_week": [1, 3], "end_date": "2026-12-31"}

| Field | Description | |---|---| | frequency | daily, weekly, or monthly | | interval | Repeat every N periods (default 1) | | days_of_week | For weekly recurrence: which days (0=Monday … 6=Sunday) | | end_date | Optional date after which the trigger stops recurring |

After a recurring trigger fires, it is automatically advanced to its next occurrence rather than being marked complete.

Agent Usage

Your AI agent can schedule a trigger the same way it creates a normal entry, by adding action_type/target_uuid (and mode/recurrence if needed):

calendar_tool(
  date="2026-08-01", time="09:00", title="Weekly follow-up campaign",
  action_type="campaign_start", target_uuid="",
  recurrence='{"frequency":"weekly","interval":1}'
)
target_uuid is the workflow UUID for workflow_run triggers, or the campaign UUID for campaign_start/campaign_pause triggers.

documents.title: Call History
documents.excerpt: Allow your AI agent to search past conversation history across calls, web calls, and text chats to provide personalized service.
documents.content:
The Call History tool enables your AI agent to look up past interactions with a caller across all channels — phone calls, web calls, and text chats. This helps the agent recognize returning customers, recall previous issues, and provide personalized service.

How It Works

The Call History tool searches your organization's past WorkflowRun records:

  1. Automatic Caller Detection: The tool always includes the current caller's phone number in the search automatically
  2. LLM-Provided Search: The agent can also search by customer name, keywords, or an alternative phone number
  3. Multi-Channel Results: Results include past calls, web calls, and text chat interactions
  4. Rich Context: Each result includes call metadata, disposition, gathered context, and transcript availability

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Max Results: Maximum number of past records to return (1–50, default 10). Keep this small so the agent sees only the most relevant recent interactions.
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes

Agent Usage

Search by Customer Name

call_history(query="Yusuf Bülbül")

Search by Topic or Keyword

call_history(query="refund request")

Search by Phone Number

call_history(phone_number="+905551234567")

Combined Search

call_history(query="invoice dispute", phone_number="+905551234567")

Returned Data

Each matching record includes:

  • Run ID & Name: Unique identifier and name of the workflow run
  • Workflow Name: Which assistant handled the interaction
  • Call Type & Mode: Inbound call, outbound call, web call, or text chat
  • State & Completion: Whether the interaction completed successfully
  • Created At: When the interaction occurred
  • Caller/Called Numbers: Phone numbers involved
  • Direction: Inbound or outbound
  • Disposition: Call outcome (e.g., "completed", "transferred")
  • Has Transcript: Whether a transcript is available
  • Annotations & Gathered Context: Any data extracted or annotated during the call
Common scenarios:
  • Recognizing a returning customer who mentions their name
  • Recalling a previous issue the caller references
  • Checking if the caller has called about the same problem before
  • Providing context-aware service when the caller is on a different phone number
  • Looking up past orders or support tickets mentioned in previous conversations

documents.title: Call Transfer
documents.excerpt: Enable your AI agent to transfer calls to phone numbers or SIP endpoints with built-in call transfer functionality.
documents.content:
The Call Transfer tool enables your AI agent to transfer active calls to phone numbers or SIP endpoints. When configured, your agent can seamlessly transfer callers to human operators, departments, or other systems while maintaining a professional experience.

Supported Providers

Call transfer is available for telephony calls using Twilio, Telnyx, Asterisk ARI, or Asterisk SIP Trunk providers. Web calls do not support transfer functionality.

How It Works

The Call Transfer tool performs blind transfers where no call context is shared with the destination. Here's what happens:

  1. Agent Decision: Your AI agent determines a transfer is needed and calls the transfer function
  2. Pre-transfer Message: (Optional) Agent plays a custom message like "Let me transfer you to our sales team"
  3. Hold Experience: Caller hears hold music while the transfer is processed
  4. Connection: Once the destination answers, the caller is connected directly
  5. Agent Handoff: The AI agent ends its involvement in the call

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Destination: Phone number or SIP endpoint (see formats below)
  • Timeout: How long to wait for destination to answer (default 30 seconds)
  • Pre-transfer Message: Optional custom message played before transfer

Destination Formats

For Twilio:

  • Phone numbers: E.164 format: +1234567890
  • Must be a valid reachable phone number
For Telnyx:
  • Phone numbers: E.164 format: +1234567890
  • Must be a valid reachable phone number
For Asterisk ARI (generic, no SIP trunk configured):
  • SIP endpoints only: PJSIP/extension or SIP/endpoint
  • Examples: PJSIP/sales-queue, SIP/1001, PJSIP/conference-room
For Asterisk SIP Trunk:
  • SIP endpoints: PJSIP/extension or SIP/endpoint for internal transfers
  • Phone numbers: E.164 format: +1234567890 — routed out through the
organization's configured SIP trunk (e.g. NetGSM, Verimor, or any standards-compliant carrier) to reach GSM/mobile and other PSTN numbers
  • Must be a valid, reachable phone number for your trunk provider
Generic Asterisk ARI configs (no SIP Trunk configured) only support transferring to SIP endpoints. To transfer to GSM/PSTN phone numbers over Asterisk, configure a SIP Trunk telephony configuration for your organization — see SIP Trunk setup.

Setup Requirements

  1. Organization Setup: Ensure your organization has a supported telephony provider configured
  2. Tool Enablement: Add the Call Transfer tool to your agent's available tools
  3. Destination Validation:
- Twilio: Verify phone numbers are reachable - Telnyx: Verify phone numbers are reachable - ARI: Verify SIP endpoints exist on your Asterisk server - SIP Trunk: Verify SIP endpoints exist on your Asterisk server, or that phone numbers are reachable through your configured trunk
  1. Testing: Test transfers in your specific provider environment

Troubleshooting

  • Destination not reachable: Verify destination number/endpoint is valid and reachable
  • Tool not available: Check that Call Transfer tool is added to the correct agent node
  • Transfer failures: Handle transfer failure scenarios within your agent prompts

documents.title: End Call
documents.excerpt: Allow your AI agent to terminate calls when conversations reach a natural conclusion or specific conditions are met.
documents.content:
The End Call tool enables your AI agent to terminate calls programmatically when conversations reach a natural conclusion, specific conditions are met, or when instructed by the caller.

How It Works

The End Call tool provides a clean way to terminate conversations:

  1. Agent Decision: Your AI agent determines the call should end based on conversation context
  2. Optional Message: Agent can provide a closing message before ending the call
  3. Clean Termination: Call is terminated gracefully through the telephony provider
  4. Call Disposition: Call disposition is updated in the system

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • End Message: Optional closing message played before termination
  • Reason: Optional reason code for call termination tracking

Agent Usage

Your AI agent can end calls during conversations:

end_call(message="Thank you for calling. Have a great day!", reason="conversation_complete")

Common scenarios:

  • Conversation has reached natural conclusion
