  • User explicitly requests to end the call
  • Agent has completed all requested tasks
  • Call timeout or error conditions

documents.title: Incoming Messages
documents.excerpt: Allow your AI agent to search inbound WhatsApp, Telegram, and Instagram messages received through your configured chat channels.
documents.content:
The Incoming Messages tool lets your AI agent look up inbound messages your organization has received through its connected chat channels — WhatsApp, Telegram, and Instagram — within a date range.

How It Works

The tool searches the messages Verasist has already recorded for your organization's chat channels:

  1. Date Range: The agent supplies a start and end date/time (date-only values are accepted; the end date includes the full day)
  2. Optional Filters: Channel type, exact sender identity, and result limit
  3. Sender Details: Results include the sender's display name (when the provider supplies one) and phone number for WhatsApp senders

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Channel: Optionally restrict results to a single configured channel; leave unset to search across all channels
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes

Agent Usage

incoming_messages(start_date="2026-07-20", end_date="2026-07-21", channel_type="whatsapp", limit=20)
  • start_date / end_date — required, ISO 8601 (date-only values accepted)
  • channel_type — optional filter: telegram, whatsapp, or instagram
  • sender_identity — optional exact sender filter
  • limit — optional, 1–200 (default 50)
Common scenarios:
  • Checking whether a customer already messaged in about an issue before calling
  • Reviewing recent inbound messages during a shift handoff
  • Looking up a specific sender's message history across channels
For WhatsApp results, the agent is instructed to always surface both the phone number and sender name (when available) so you can identify the customer.

documents.title: Send Message
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent send a WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram message through a configured chat channel during a live conversation.
documents.content:
The Send Message tool lets your AI agent send a text message to the caller (or a third party) through one of your organization's configured chat channels — WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram — without leaving the live conversation.

This tool sends through a channel you've already connected under Channels. Configure the channel first, then create the Send Message tool and point it at that channel.

How It Works

The channel is fixed when you configure the tool — you pick one connected WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram channel. At call time, the LLM only supplies:

  1. Target Identity: Who to send the message to, in the format expected by that channel
  2. Message: The text content to send
Verasist resolves the channel configuration for your organization, validates it, and sends the message through that channel's provider.

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Channel: Select one of your organization's configured chat channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, or Instagram). Only chat-capable channels appear in this list — configure one under Channels first if none are available.
  • Custom Message: Optional message (text or audio) played to the caller before the tool executes

Agent Usage

The LLM calls the tool with a recipient identity and message text. The expected identity format depends on the selected channel:

| Channel | Target Identity Format | |---------|-------------------------| | WhatsApp | Phone number in E.164 format, e.g. +14155552671 | | Telegram | Telegram chat ID (numeric or string) | | Instagram | Instagram-scoped user ID (IGSID) — a numeric string |

send_message(target_identity="+14155552671", message="Here's the confirmation link you asked for: https://example.com/confirm")

Common scenarios:

  • Caller asks you to text them a confirmation, receipt, or summary
  • Sending a link or document reference that's easier to read than to say aloud
  • Following up with a written recap after a phone or web call

Returned Data

After sending, the tool reports back to the agent:

  • Status: Whether the send succeeded
  • Message ID: The provider's message identifier, when available
  • Channel Type: Which channel the message was sent through
  • Target: The normalized recipient identity used
If the channel isn't configured, isn't found for your organization, or the provider rejects the send, the tool returns an error to the agent instead of failing the call — the conversation continues.

The tool only sends through the single channel selected at configuration time. To send through a different channel (e.g. Telegram instead of WhatsApp), create a separate Send Message tool pointed at that channel.

documents.title: Transfer to Assistant
documents.excerpt: Enable your AI agent to transfer the current conversation to another workflow or assistant with full context handoff.
documents.content:
The Transfer to Assistant tool lets your AI agent hand off the current conversation to another workflow (assistant) within your organization. The target assistant receives the caller's context and a conversation summary, starting fresh from its beginning node.

How It Works

Unlike Call Transfer which transfers to an external phone number, Transfer to Assistant redirects the conversation to another AI workflow within Verasist:

  1. Agent Decision: The AI agent determines the caller needs a different assistant (e.g., sales → support)
  2. Summary Generation: The agent creates a concise summary of the conversation so far
  3. Context Merge: Current call context is merged with any configured variable mappings and passed to the target
  4. Transition: The target assistant's start node becomes active, and the conversation continues seamlessly

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Target Workflow UUID: The UUID of the destination workflow/assistant to transfer to
  • Transfer Message: Optional message played to the caller before the transfer (e.g., "Let me transfer you to our billing department")
  • Initial Context Mapping: Optional key-value mapping to rename context variables for the target assistant
- Example: {"customer_name": "caller_name"} copies customer_name from the current context into caller_name for the target
  • Custom Message: Optional pre-recorded audio message before transfer

Context Handoff

The target assistant automatically receives:

  • All existing initial_context variables
  • All gathered_context variables
  • transfer_summary — the agent's conversation summary
  • transferred_from_workflow — the source workflow ID
  • transferred_from_run_id — the source workflow run ID
Any explicit mappings in Initial Context Mapping are applied on top of these defaults.

Agent Usage

Your AI agent transfers conversations with a summary:

transfer_to_assistant(summary="Caller is John Smith, calling about an overcharge on invoice #12345. Discussed the charges for March and April. Needs billing to issue a refund.")

Common scenarios:

  • Caller needs to speak to a different department (sales → support, support → billing)
  • Conversation topic changes and requires a specialized assistant
  • Escalation to a supervisor workflow
  • Multi-step processes where different assistants handle different stages
Transfer to Assistant only works between workflows within the same organization. For external phone transfers, use the Call Transfer tool.

documents.title: Transfer to Channel
documents.excerpt: Hand off a live voice call or text chat to a new conversation on a different messaging channel, carrying over the full history.
documents.content:
The Transfer to Channel tool lets your AI agent continue the current conversation on a different messaging channel — for example, moving a live phone call or WhatsApp chat over to Telegram, or starting a WhatsApp conversation for a caller who wants to keep chatting after hanging up. The destination conversation is seeded with everything discussed so far, so it doesn't start from a blank slate.

How It Works

Unlike Transfer to Assistant (which switches to a different workflow within the same conversation) or Call Transfer (a blind transfer to a phone number/SIP endpoint with no context), Transfer to Channel starts a brand-new session on another channel:

  1. Agent Decision: The AI agent determines the caller wants to continue elsewhere (e.g. "can you text me on WhatsApp instead?") and calls the tool with the recipient's identity
  2. New Session Created: A new conversation is started on the destination channel, using the target workflow configured on the tool
  3. History Carried Over: Everything said so far in the current conversation is seeded into the destination session, and it resumes from the same workflow node the source conversation was on — not the start node — so the agent's next reply picks up naturally instead of repeating a generic greeting
  4. Source Conversation Ends: Once the destination session has been created successfully, the source conversation (the live call or the original text chat) is ended. Exactly one active session remains — the transferred one.
If the destination session fails to start (invalid destination, misconfigured channel, quota exceeded, etc.), the source conversation is left untouched and continues normally.

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Destination Channel: The channel type (whatsapp, telegram, or instagram) and the specific Channel Configuration to send from
  • Target Workflow: The workflow (assistant) that should run the destination conversation
  • Custom Message: Optional message played/sent before the transfer
The destination channel and target workflow are fixed when the tool is configured — the LLM only supplies the recipient's identity at call time.

Agent Usage

Your AI agent transfers the conversation by providing the destination identity:

transfer_to_channel(target_identity="+14155550100")

The expected format for target_identity depends on the configured destination channel:

| Channel | target_identity format | |---|---| | WhatsApp | E.164 phone number, e.g. +14155550100 | | Telegram | Telegram chat ID | | Instagram | Instagram-scoped user ID |

Common scenarios:

  • Caller on a phone call asks to continue over WhatsApp/Telegram instead
  • A text-chat user asks to switch to a different messaging app
  • Business hours end for voice support but chat support should keep going
This tool ends the current conversation once the destination conversation has successfully started — the two do not run side by side. If you want both the source and destination to keep running independently, use Send Message instead, which sends a one-off message without ending the current conversation.

If the caller sends another message on the transferred channel shortly after, it re-attaches to the same transferred session rather than starting a new one — as long as the destination channel configuration's identity matches on both the outbound and inbound side (this is automatic for channels set up through Verasist).

documents.title: CRM
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent search, create, update, and list CRM contacts (HubSpot, Microsoft Dynamics 365) during live conversations.
documents.content:
The CRM tool lets your AI agent manage contacts in your organization's connected CRM — search for an existing contact, create a new one, update one, or list recent contacts — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a CRM account you've already connected under Settings → CRM. Connect the account first, then create the CRM tool and point it at that account.

Supported Providers

| Provider | Auth Type | Notes | |----------|-----------|-------| | HubSpot | OAuth 2.0 | Uses Verasist's platform HubSpot app by default — no client ID/secret needed from you | | Microsoft Dynamics 365 | OAuth 2.0 | Requires your Azure AD Tenant ID and Dynamics Instance URL |

Salesforce, Zoho CRM, and Pipedrive are listed as providers but are coming soon.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → CRM and choose Connect Account
  2. Select a provider (HubSpot or Dynamics 365)
  3. For Dynamics 365, enter your Tenant ID and Instance URL (e.g. https://yourorg.crm.dynamics.com); HubSpot needs no extra fields
  4. Complete the OAuth consent flow in the popup/redirect
  5. The connected account appears in the CRM tool's account picker when you configure the tool
Verasist automatically refreshes the OAuth access token when it expires, so long-running agent sessions keep working without re-authentication.

How It Works

The account is fixed when you configure the tool (crm_config_id) — the LLM only supplies contact details at call time. Verasist translates the standard contact fields the LLM works with into each provider's raw field names before calling the CRM:

| Standard Field | HubSpot Property | Dynamics 365 (contact) Attribute | |-----------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------| | first_name | firstname | firstname | | last_name | lastname | lastname | | email | email | emailaddress1 | | phone | phone | telephone1 | | company | company | (not mapped — requires a lookup field) | | job_title | jobtitle | jobtitle | | notes | (not mapped) | (not mapped) |

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • CRM Account: The connected HubSpot or Dynamics 365 account this tool uses
  • Allow Search: Let the agent search for a contact by email or phone (default: on)
  • Allow Create: Let the agent create a new contact (default: on)
  • Allow Update: Let the agent update an existing contact (default: on)
  • Allow List: Let the agent list recent contacts (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability (search, create, update, or list) must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Search for a Contact

crm_search_contact(email="jane@example.com")

Create a Contact

crm_create_contact(first_name="Jane", last_name="Doe", email="jane@example.com", phone="+14155552671", company="Acme Inc.")

Update a Contact

crm_update_contact(record_id="12345", phone="+14155552672")

record_id comes from a prior search, create, or list call.

List Recent Contacts

crm_list_contacts(limit=10)

Common scenarios:

  • Checking whether a caller already exists in the CRM before creating a duplicate
  • Logging a new lead captured during the call
  • Updating a contact's phone number or job title after the caller confirms it
  • Pulling up recently added contacts for a sales follow-up
The tool fails closed if the configured CRM account doesn't belong to your organization, is inactive, or its OAuth token can't be refreshed — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Email
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent send and search email through a connected Gmail or Microsoft mailbox during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Email tool lets your AI agent send an email or search/read recent email in a connected mailbox — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a mailbox you've already connected under Settings → Email. Connect the account first, then create the Email tool and point it at that mailbox.

Supported Providers

| Provider | Scopes | |----------|--------| | Gmail | gmail.send, gmail.readonly | | Microsoft (Outlook / Microsoft 365) | Mail.Read, Mail.Send, offline_access |

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → Email and choose Connect Mailbox
  2. Select Gmail or Microsoft
  3. Complete the OAuth consent flow in the popup/redirect
  4. The connected mailbox appears in the Email tool's account picker when you configure the tool

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Mailbox: The connected Gmail or Microsoft account this tool uses
  • Allow Send: Let the agent send email through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Read: Let the agent search/read email through this tool (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one of Allow Send / Allow Read must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Sending an Email

email_tool(to=["customer@example.com"], subject="Your requested confirmation", body="Here's the confirmation you asked for during our call.", cc=["sales@yourcompany.com"])

to, subject, and body are required; cc is optional.

Searching/Reading Email

email_tool_search(query="invoice", since="2026-07-01", limit=10)

All search parameters are optional — omit them to get the most recent emails in the inbox.

Common scenarios:

  • Emailing a caller a confirmation, receipt, or document they asked for
  • Looking up a prior email thread before answering a question
  • Confirming whether a previous message from the caller was received
  • Sending a written recap after a phone or web call
The tool fails closed if the configured mailbox doesn't belong to your organization, is inactive, or the provider isn't supported — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Google Calendar
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent create, check, update, and cancel events in a connected Google Calendar during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Google Calendar tool lets your AI agent create an event, list events / check availability, update an event, or cancel an event in a connected Google account — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a Google account you've already connected under Settings → Applications. Connect the account first, then create the Google Calendar tool and point it at that account.
This is a connected Google calendar, separate from Verasist's own built-in Calendar tool. Use this tool when you need the agent to read from or write to a real Google Calendar rather than Verasist's internal calendar entries.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → Applications and choose Connect Google Account
  2. Grant the calendar.events scope during the OAuth consent flow (Google Calendar, Tasks, and Sheets share the same connected Google account)
  3. The connected account appears in the Google Calendar tool's account picker when you configure the tool

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Google Account: The connected account this tool uses
  • Allow Create: Let the agent create events through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow List: Let the agent list events / check availability through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Update: Let the agent update events through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Cancel: Let the agent cancel events through this tool (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Creating an Event

google_calendar_tool(summary="Consultation with Jane Doe", start="2026-07-22T10:00:00-07:00", end="2026-07-22T10:30:00-07:00", attendees=["jane@example.com"])

summary, start, and end are required (RFC 3339 date/times).

Listing Events / Checking Availability

google_calendar_tool_list(time_min="2026-07-22T00:00:00-07:00", time_max="2026-07-22T23:59:59-07:00")

Updating an Event

google_calendar_tool_update(event_id="abc123", start="2026-07-22T11:00:00-07:00", end="2026-07-22T11:30:00-07:00")

Cancelling an Event

google_calendar_tool_cancel(event_id="abc123")

event_id comes from a prior list or create call.

Common scenarios:

  • Booking an appointment directly on a real Google Calendar during the call
  • Checking availability before offering a time slot
  • Rescheduling or cancelling an existing meeting the caller mentions
The tool fails closed if the configured Google account doesn't belong to your organization or is inactive — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Google Sheets
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent append, read, and update rows in a connected Google Sheet during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Google Sheets tool lets your AI agent append a new row, read a range of rows, or overwrite a specific row in a fixed Google Sheet — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a Google account you've already connected under Settings → Applications. Connect the account first, then create the Google Sheets tool and point it at that account and spreadsheet.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → Applications and choose Connect Google Account
  2. Grant the spreadsheets scope during the OAuth consent flow (Google Sheets, Tasks, and Calendar share the same connected Google account)
  3. When configuring the tool, provide the target Spreadsheet ID (from the sheet's URL) and Sheet/Tab Name (defaults to Sheet1)

How It Works

The Google account and the target spreadsheet/tab are both fixed when you configure the tool — the LLM only supplies row values or a lookup range at call time. All operations resolve to A1-notation ranges within the configured sheet/tab.

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Google Account: The connected account this tool uses
  • Spreadsheet ID: The fixed target spreadsheet (copy the ID from the sheet's URL, e.g. https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d//edit)
  • Sheet Name: The fixed target tab within the spreadsheet (default Sheet1)
  • Allow Append: Let the agent append rows through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Read: Let the agent read rows through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Update: Let the agent overwrite a row through this tool (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Appending a Row

google_sheets_tool(values=["Jane Doe", "jane@example.com", "+14155552671", "Interested in premium plan"])

values is an ordered list of cell values, left to right.

Reading Rows

google_sheets_tool_read(range="A1:D20")

range is optional — omit it to read the whole sheet.

Updating a Row

google_sheets_tool_update(row=5, values=["Jane Doe", "jane@example.com", "+14155552672", "Upgraded to premium"])

row is the 1-based row number to overwrite (e.g. 2 for the row right after headers).

Common scenarios:

  • Logging a new lead or call outcome to a shared spreadsheet
  • Looking up existing rows to check whether an entry already exists
  • Correcting or updating a row after the caller confirms new details
The tool fails closed if the configured Google account doesn't belong to your organization or is inactive — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Google Tasks
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent create, list, and complete tasks in a connected Google Tasks account during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Google Tasks tool lets your AI agent create a task, list existing tasks, or mark a task complete in a connected Google account — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a Google account you've already connected under Settings → Applications. Connect the account first, then create the Google Tasks tool and point it at that account.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → Applications and choose Connect Google Account
  2. Grant the tasks scope during the OAuth consent flow (Google Tasks, Calendar, and Sheets share the same connected Google account)
  3. The connected account appears in the Google Tasks tool's account picker when you configure the tool

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Google Account: The connected account this tool uses
  • Allow Create: Let the agent create tasks through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow List: Let the agent list tasks through this tool (default: on)
  • Allow Complete: Let the agent mark tasks completed through this tool (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Creating a Task

google_tasks_tool(title="Call back Jane Doe", notes="Follow up about the refund request", due="2026-07-22T00:00:00.000Z")

Only title is required.

Listing Tasks

google_tasks_tool_list(show_completed=false, limit=10)

Completing a Task

google_tasks_tool_complete(task_id="abc123")

task_id comes from a prior list or create call.

Common scenarios:

  • Adding a follow-up action item the caller requested
  • Checking off a task once the caller confirms it's done
  • Reviewing open tasks before starting a call
The tool fails closed if the configured Google account doesn't belong to your organization or is inactive — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Trendyol
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent answer customer questions, check order status, and manage returns on your connected Trendyol seller account during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Trendyol tool lets your AI agent handle common seller-side tasks on Trendyol — listing and answering customer questions, checking order status, and reviewing returned/claimed orders — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a Trendyol seller account you've already connected under Settings → E-Commerce. Connect the account first, then create the Trendyol tool and point it at that account.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → E-Commerce and choose Connect Trendyol
  2. Enter your Supplier ID, API Key, and API Secret (from your Trendyol Seller Center integration credentials)
  3. Choose the Environment: production or stage
  4. Choose which order statuses to subscribe to for webhook notifications (defaults to all): CREATED, PICKING, INVOICED, SHIPPED, CANCELLED, DELIVERED, UNDELIVERED, RETURNED, UNSUPPLIED, AWAITING, UNPACKED, AT_COLLECTION_POINT, VERIFIED
  5. Verasist registers a webhook with Trendyol so order status updates arrive automatically

How It Works

The account is fixed when you configure the tool (trendyol_config_id) — the LLM only supplies question/order details at call time.

  • Questions and claims (list, detail, answer, list claims, issue reasons, claim item audits) call the Trendyol API live, using your stored Supplier ID/API Key/API Secret
  • Order status is not fetched live — it's read from the latest webhook event Verasist has stored locally for that order number. This keeps order lookups instant during a call, but means status is only as fresh as the last webhook Trendyol has delivered for that order

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Trendyol Account: The connected seller account this tool uses
  • Allow List Questions: Let the agent list customer questions (default: on)
  • Allow Get Question Detail: Let the agent fetch a single question's full detail (default: on)
  • Allow Answer Questions: Let the agent submit an answer to a question (default: on)
  • Allow Check Order Status: Let the agent check an order's latest known status (default: on)
  • Allow List Claims: Let the agent list returned/claimed orders (default: on)
  • Allow Get Claim Issue Reasons: Let the agent fetch the global list of claim issue/rejection reasons (default: on)
  • Allow Get Claim Item Audits: Let the agent fetch the status/audit history of a single claim item (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability must be enabled.

Agent Usage

List Customer Questions

trendyol_list_questions(status="WAITING_FOR_ANSWER", limit=10)

Optional filters: status (WAITING_FOR_ANSWER, ANSWERED, REJECTED, REPORTED), barcode.

Get Question Detail

trendyol_question_detail(question_id="123456")

Answer a Question

trendyol_answer_question(question_id="123456", answer_text="Your order ships within 24 hours of confirmation.")

Answer text must be 10–2000 characters.

Check Order Status

trendyol_order_status(order_number="TY123456789")

List Returns/Claims

trendyol_list_claims(status="Created", limit=10)

Claim Issue Reasons & Audits

trendyol_claim_issue_reasons()
trendyol_claim_item_audits(claim_item_id="789")

Common scenarios:

  • A customer calls asking whether their unanswered question has a response yet
  • The agent answers a routine customer question directly during the call
  • A caller wants to know if their order has shipped
  • Reviewing why a return was rejected or checking a claim's audit trail
The tool fails closed if the configured Trendyol account doesn't belong to your organization or is inactive — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: Yemek Sepeti
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent look up, update, and list orders on your connected Yemek Sepeti (Delivery Hero) partner account during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Yemek Sepeti tool lets your AI agent handle restaurant-side order operations on Yemek Sepeti — fetching order detail, updating order status, and listing recent orders — all during a live conversation.

This tool acts through a Yemek Sepeti partner account you've already connected under Settings → E-Commerce. Connect the account first, then create the Yemek Sepeti tool and point it at that account.

Connecting an Account

  1. Go to Settings → E-Commerce and choose Connect Yemek Sepeti
  2. Enter your Chain ID, Client ID, and Client Secret (from your Yemek Sepeti / Delivery Hero partner integration credentials)
  3. Optionally enter a specific Vendor ID to scope the connection to a single store
  4. Verasist generates a webhook URL and secret you can register with Yemek Sepeti for order notifications

How It Works

The account is fixed when you configure the tool (yemeksepeti_config_id) — the LLM only supplies order details at call time. All operations (order detail, status update, list) call the Yemek Sepeti API live using your stored Chain ID/Client ID/Client Secret (and Vendor ID, if set).

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Yemek Sepeti Account: The connected partner account this tool uses
  • Allow Get Order Detail: Let the agent fetch a single order's full detail (default: on)
  • Allow Update Order Status: Let the agent change an order's status (default: on)
  • Allow List Orders: Let the agent list recent orders (default: on)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes
At least one capability must be enabled.

Agent Usage

Get Order Detail

yemeksepeti_get_order_detail(order_id="ORD-12345")

Update Order Status

yemeksepeti_update_order_status(order_id="ORD-12345", status="DISPATCHED")

Allowed status values: READY_FOR_PICKUP, DISPATCHED, CANCELLED. When cancelling, provide a cancellation_reason: CLOSED, ITEM_UNAVAILABLE, or TOO_BUSY.

yemeksepeti_update_order_status(order_id="ORD-12345", status="CANCELLED", cancellation_reason="ITEM_UNAVAILABLE")

List Recent Orders

yemeksepeti_list_orders(start_time="2026-07-20T00:00:00Z", end_time="2026-07-21T00:00:00Z", limit=20)

Common scenarios:

  • A courier or customer calls to check the status of an order
  • Marking an order as ready for pickup or dispatched while on the phone with a courier
  • Cancelling an order because an item is unavailable
  • Reviewing a batch of recent orders during a shift handoff call
The tool fails closed if the configured Yemek Sepeti account doesn't belong to your organization or is inactive — the agent receives a clear error and the conversation continues instead of failing the call.

documents.title: HTTP API
documents.excerpt: Create REST API tools that your AI agent can invoke during conversations to integrate with external systems.
documents.content:
HTTP API tools allow you to attach extrernal REST API calls directly to workflow nodes, enabling your voice agents to call any internal or external system during live conversations based on LLM judgment and your prompts. This works similar to function calling on any agentic platform and is 100% open source and fully customizable.

Video Tutorial

What is an HTTP API Tool?

An HTTP API Tool is a REST API definition that the LLM can invoke at runtime.

Typical use cases:

  • Call your own backend endpoints
  • Trigger n8n automations
  • Sync data with a CRM
  • Fetch data from external APIs (weather, pricing, availability, etc.)
  • Write/update/read data using Rest API
The LLM decides:
  • which tool to call
  • when to call it
  • what parameters to send
All based on:
  • Your prompts: node-level instructions in simple english (or any language)
  • Tool name
  • Tool description
  • Parameter definitions

Defining an HTTP API Tool

1. Tool Name

  • Must be clear and action-oriented.
  • Examples: capture_lead_interest, fetch_weather, 'create_crm_contact', etc

2. Tool Description

  • Extremely important
  • This is how the LLM decides when to use the tool.
  • Write it in plain, explicit English.
Bad: "API to capture data"

Good: "This tool is to capture interest. Use this tool when the user clearly expresses interest in the product or wants to be contacted"

3. Endpoint Configuration

  • Full URL (must include http:// or https://)
  • Supports REST methods
Common mistake: forgetting https:// in the URL.

4. Authentication & Headers

  • Add custom authentication
  • Add custom headers
  • Works with internal services and third-party APIs

5. Parameters

Each parameter must have:

  • Name
  • Type
  • Description
  • Required/Optional flag
Parameter descriptions matter more than types.

Guidelines:

  • Start with string parameters when possible
  • Be explicit in what the value represents
  • Mark only truly mandatory fields as required
Example:
  • interest (string):
"Set to true if the user clearly shows intent to buy or wants follow-up. Otherwise false."


Attaching Tools to Workflow Nodes

  • You can attach multiple tools to a single node
  • All the tools that you have created will be available for selection in the node
  • Tools are only callable when attached to that node
  • The LLM will choose which one to call
Inside the node, guide the LLM using simple English instructions.

Example:

"If the user shows interest in speaking to sales or wants a callback, immediately call the capture_lead_interest tool and set interest to true." This instruction is often the deciding factor for correct tool usage.

This instruction is often the deciding factor for correct tool usage.


Tool Invocation Logic (How the LLM Thinks)

The LLM considers:

  • User's spoken intent
  • Node prompt instructions
  • Tool name and description
  • Parameter descriptions
If these align clearly, the tool is called automatically.

Poor naming or vague descriptions lead to:

  • Missed tool calls
  • Wrong parameters
  • Hallucinated values

Key Best Practices

  • Name tools clearly
  • Write detailed, action-based descriptions
  • Keep parameters simple at first
  • Always include http/https in URLs
  • Use plain English in node instructions
  • Attach only relevant tools to each node
Well-defined tools + clear prompts = reliable, production-grade voice agents.

documents.title: MCP Tool
documents.excerpt: Connect an external MCP server to your voice agent so the LLM can call remote tools during a live conversation.
documents.content:
This page is about using an external MCP server as a tool inside a voice agent. If you want Claude, Cursor, or another coding agent to control Verasist itself over MCP, see Verasist MCP Server.
You can also ask the Automation Assistant (the chat assistant on the Automation page) to create an MCP tool for you — give it the server URL and, if needed, the credential to use — and it will wire the resulting tool into the agent it's building.

MCP tools let a Verasist voice agent call tools exposed by a remote Model Context Protocol server during a live conversation. Verasist discovers the remote tool catalog, turns those tools into LLM-callable functions, and forwards invocations to the MCP server over authenticated Streamable HTTP.

What to configure

An MCP tool in Verasist has four important pieces:

  • Name: the server label shown in Verasist
  • Description: tells the LLM when this MCP server is relevant
  • URL: the remote MCP server endpoint (http:// or https://)
  • Credential: the auth Verasist should send when connecting to that server
You can also set a tool filter to allow only specific remote MCP tools to be exposed.

Authentication

Most hosted MCP servers expect:

Authorization: Bearer

So before creating the MCP tool, create a credential in Verasist with:

  • Credential Type: Bearer Token
  • Token: the access token issued by your MCP server
Then select that credential on the MCP tool.
If the remote MCP server documentation says to use Bearer auth, choose Bearer Token in the credential dialog. Verasist will translate that into the exact Authorization: Bearer header on the MCP connection.

Verasist also supports other credential types, but Bearer Token is the default thing to try for third-party MCP servers unless their docs say otherwise.

How it works

The runtime path is:

  1. When you save or refresh the MCP tool, Verasist opens a short-lived authenticated MCP session and fetches the remote tool catalog.
  2. Verasist stores that catalog as the tool's discovered tools so the UI can show you which remote functions exist.
  3. When a call starts, Verasist opens one live MCP session per attached MCP server and reuses your selected credential for that session.
  4. For each node, Verasist exposes only the MCP tools allowed by the server-level filter and the node-level selection.
  5. Verasist namespaces those remote tools into ordinary LLM function definitions so they can safely coexist with HTTP API tools, call transfer, end call, and other tools.
  6. During the conversation, the LLM sees only the tool name, description, and argument schema. It does not see the secret.
  7. When the LLM calls one of those tools, Verasist forwards the invocation to the MCP server over the active authenticated session, receives the result, and feeds that result back into the agent turn.
In short: Verasist handles discovery, authentication, session management, tool registration, and result plumbing; the LLM only decides when to call the tool and with which arguments.

Creating an MCP tool

  1. Go to Tools and create a new tool.
  2. Choose MCP Server.
  3. Enter a clear name and a description that explains when the LLM should use this server.
  4. Paste the MCP server URL.
  5. Select the credential. In most cases this should be a Bearer Token credential.
  6. Save the tool and confirm that Verasist discovered the remote tools.
If the server exposes many tools, use filtering to keep only the ones your agent actually needs.

Refreshing the tool catalog

If the remote MCP server adds, removes, or changes its tools after you've already created the tool, you don't need to recreate it:

  1. Open the MCP tool in Tools.
  2. Trigger a refresh to re-discover the remote catalog.
  3. Verasist reconnects to the server and replaces the stored discovered tools with the current catalog.
If the remote server is unreachable when you refresh, Verasist keeps the previously discovered tools intact instead of clearing them — a failed refresh never leaves the tool without a usable catalog.

Attaching it to a node

After the MCP tool is created:

  1. Open the workflow node where the tool should be available.
  2. Add the MCP tool from the node's tool list.
  3. Select only the remote MCP functions that should be callable on that node.
  4. In the node prompt, tell the LLM exactly when to use those functions.
The tighter the node-level selection and prompt guidance, the more reliable MCP tool usage becomes.

Best practices

  • Use one MCP server per logical integration when possible.
  • Keep the tool description explicit about when the LLM should use that server.
  • Expose only the minimum remote functions needed for each node.
  • Prefer a Bearer Token credential unless the MCP server specifies another auth scheme.
  • Test discovery first, then test a real phone/web call to confirm the LLM invokes the right MCP function with the right arguments.
If the remote MCP server is temporarily unavailable, Verasist degrades gracefully and the call can continue without those MCP tools rather than crashing the entire conversation.

documents.title: Web Page Query
documents.excerpt: Let your AI agent fetch public web pages and read their clean text content during live conversations.
documents.content:
The Web Page Query tool lets your AI agent fetch one or more public web pages and extract clean, readable text — article body, product catalog listings, or general page content — during a live conversation.

How It Works

  1. Fetch: Verasist requests the page(s) over HTTP(S), enforcing a response size limit and timeout
  2. Extract: Boilerplate (navigation, footers, scripts) is stripped, and the readable content is extracted — using article extraction first, then a structured JSON-LD catalog parser, then a generic HTML text fallback
  3. Return: The cleaned text (up to 100,000 characters) is returned to the agent to summarize or answer questions from

Configuration

Basic Settings

  • Fixed URL (optional): Pin the tool to a single public URL. If set, the agent doesn't need to supply a URL when calling the tool. If left empty, the agent must supply one or more URLs itself
  • Max Results: Maximum number of pages the agent can fetch in a single call (1–50, default 10)
  • Custom Message: Optional message played to the caller before the tool executes

Agent Usage

If no fixed URL is configured, the agent supplies the URL(s) to fetch:

web_page_query(urls=["https://example.com/faq"])

Multiple URLs are fetched in parallel, up to the configured max:

web_page_query(urls=["https://example.com/products/1", "https://example.com/products/2"], max_results=2)

If a fixed URL is configured, the agent can call the tool with no arguments and it fetches that URL automatically.

Common scenarios:

  • Reading a public FAQ or policy page to answer a caller's question
  • Checking current pricing or product listings from a public catalog page
  • Pulling the latest content from a status or announcements page
Only public http(s) URLs are supported — this tool cannot access authenticated pages, internal systems, or APIs. For calling an authenticated API, use an HTTP API tool instead.

documents.title: Knowledge Base
documents.excerpt: Upload documents that your voice agent can reference during live conversations to provide accurate, context-aware responses.
documents.content:
The Knowledge Base lets you upload documents that your voice agents can reference during conversations. Instead of encoding all information into prompts, you can provide source documents and let the agent retrieve relevant content on the fly.

An embedding API key (configured in AI Models Configuration → Embedding) is required for Chunked Search mode. Full Document mode does not require embeddings.

How It Works

  1. You upload a document (PDF, Word, TXT, JSON, CSV, or Excel) to the Knowledge Base
  2. You choose a retrieval mode — Full Document or Chunked Search
  3. Verasist processes the document based on the selected mode
  4. You attach the document to one or more workflow nodes
  5. During a call, the agent retrieves information from the document and uses it to generate accurate responses

Supported File Types

| Format | Extension | |-------------|-------------------| | PDF | .pdf | | Word | .docx, .doc | | Text | .txt | | JSON | .json | | CSV | .csv | | Excel | .xlsx |

Maximum file size: 5 MB

CSV and Excel files are treated as tabular data — in Full Document mode the agent can look up an exact row/column or append/edit rows (see Full Document: Search, Edit, and Add below) instead of receiving the whole spreadsheet as text.

Uploading Documents

  1. Go to Knowledge Base Files in the dashboard
  2. Click Upload New or drag and drop a file
  3. Choose a retrieval mode (see below)
  4. Click Upload & Process — the document will be processed according to the selected mode
You can also upload a document directly from the Automation Assistant (the chat assistant on the Automation page) using the attach button next to the message box — it uses the same Knowledge Base storage, and the file will also show up under Knowledge Base Files. Ask the assistant to attach it to the agent it's building and it will include the document's UUID on the relevant node for you.

Retrieval Modes

When uploading a document, you choose how the agent retrieves information from it:

The entire document text is provided to the agent whenever it queries the knowledge base. No chunking or embedding is performed.

Best for: menus, price lists, FAQs, short reference sheets, and any document where the agent needs access to all the information at once.

Full Document mode does not require an embedding API key. The document is split into smaller chunks and indexed with vector embeddings. When the agent queries the knowledge base, only the most relevant chunks are returned.

Best for: large documents like policies, manuals, or contracts where only a portion is relevant to any given question.

Attaching Documents to Nodes

Once a document is processed, you can attach it to any Start Call or Agent node in your workflow:

  1. Open the node edit dialog
  2. Scroll to the Knowledge Base Documents section
  3. Select one or more documents for the agent to reference
The agent will only search documents attached to the current node, so attach only the documents relevant to that conversation step.

Full Document: Search, Edit, and Add

For documents in Full Document mode, attaching them to a node gives the agent two functions instead of one: it can both read (search/look up) and write (edit/add to) the document during the call — useful for things like updating a shared availability sheet or logging entries directly into a CSV/XLSX file. Chunked Search documents are read-only and are never affected by the write function below.

The write function is registered automatically alongside search whenever a Full Document is attached to a node — there is no separate toggle to enable it.

Searching (retrieve_from_knowledge_base)

Instead of dumping the entire file into the prompt, the agent retrieves a small, targeted excerpt:

  • Spreadsheets (CSV/XLSX): look up an exact row with row_index (0-based), or filter with column_name + query to match a value in a specific column
  • Text-like documents (PDF/Word/TXT/Markdown): pass a query keyword/topic and the agent gets the matching section plus ~100 surrounding lines (labeled with line numbers); if that's not enough, it calls the function again with start_line/end_line to keep reading forward or backward in the same document
  • Multiple documents attached: pass document_name (filename or a distinctive substring) to target a specific one

Editing and Adding (write_to_knowledge_base)

  • Spreadsheets (CSV/XLSX):
- Edit a cell: row_index + column_name + value - Append a new row: new_row (an object of column name → value pairs) - Add a new column: column_name (optionally with a default value to backfill existing rows)
  • Text-like documents:
- Append text to the end: text - Insert text at a specific position: text + line_number (1-based, inserts before that line)
  • Multiple documents attached: pass document_name to target the right one
Writes happen directly on the stored document with no undo — use clear node prompts to guide the agent on when it's appropriate to modify a document versus only reading from it.

Best Practices

  • Use Full Document for small reference files — menus, price lists, and FAQs work best when the agent sees the entire document
  • Use Chunked Search for large documents — policies, manuals, and contracts are too large to fit in context, so chunked retrieval finds the relevant sections
  • Keep documents focused — a single topic per document produces better retrieval results than a large multi-topic file
  • Use clear, structured content — headings, lists, and short paragraphs help the chunking process
  • Attach selectively — only attach documents relevant to a specific node rather than attaching everything everywhere
  • Keep documents up to date — re-upload when source information changes to avoid stale answers

documents.title: Start Call
documents.excerpt: Configure how your AI agent answers an inbound call or opens an outbound call — greetings, pre-call data, and the initial prompt.
documents.content:
The Start Call node is the entry point for every workflow. It defines what happens when a call first connects: how the agent greets the caller, whether to fetch external data before speaking, and what tools are available during the opening turn.

You should have only one Start Call node per Voice Agent.

Configuration

Name

A short identifier shown on the canvas and in call logs (e.g., "Welcome").

Greeting

How the agent opens the conversation. You can use either a text prompt or a pre-recorded audio file.

  • Text Greeting: A prompt that the TTS engine reads aloud. Supports {{template_variables}}.
  Hi {{first_name}}, this is Sarah from Acme Corp. How can I help you today?
  • Audio Greeting: Select a pre-recorded audio file from your uploaded recordings. Useful for consistent branded greetings.

Prompt

The system prompt for the opening turn. The LLM uses this to guide the initial exchange — gathering the caller's name, reason for calling, etc. Supports {{template_variables}} from pre-call fetch or default context.

Delayed Start

When enabled, the agent waits before speaking after the call connects. Useful for outbound calls where the called party needs a moment after answering.

  • Delay Duration: Seconds to wait (0.1–10, default 2.0).

Pre-Call Data Fetch

When enabled, Verasist makes a POST request to your external API before the agent speaks. The JSON response is merged into the call context and available as {{template_variables}}.

  • Endpoint URL: Your API endpoint that receives caller information
  • Authentication: Optional credential UUID for authenticated requests
See Pre-Call Data Fetch for full details.

Tools & Documents

  • Tool UUIDs: Tools the agent can invoke during the opening turn (e.g., Call History to look up the caller)
  • Document UUIDs: Knowledge base documents the agent can reference

Extraction

When enabled, runs an LLM extraction pass at the end of the opening turn to capture structured variables (e.g., caller name, reason for call). These variables become available as {{template_variables}} in subsequent nodes.

Allow Interruption

When enabled, the caller can interrupt the agent's greeting. Disable this for outbound calls where you want the greeting to play uninterrupted.

documents.title: End Call
documents.excerpt: Configure how your AI agent closes the conversation and terminates the call — final messages, data extraction, and call disposition.
documents.content:
The End Call node is a terminal node that closes the conversation and hangs up. A workflow can have multiple End Call nodes, each reached via different edge conditions — for example, one for a successful close and another for a polite decline.

An End Call node terminates the call. A workflow can have multiple End Call nodes for different ending scenarios.

Configuration

Name

A short identifier shown in call logs. Should describe the ending context (e.g., "Successful Close", "Caller Hung Up", "Voicemail Detected").

Prompt

The system prompt for the closing exchange. The LLM uses this to deliver the final message before hanging up. 
Thank the caller for their time, summarize any next steps, and end the call warmly.

Supports {{template_variables}} from extraction or pre-call fetch.

Add Global Prompt

When enabled and a Global node exists, prepends the persona/tone instructions to this node's prompt.

Extraction

When enabled, runs a final LLM extraction pass before hangup to capture structured variables from the entire conversation:
  • Extraction Prompt: Overall instructions for what to extract
  • Extraction Variables: Each variable declares a name, data type, and extraction hint
Common extraction examples:
  • Call disposition ("successful", "declined", "needs_followup")
  • Call summary or key takeaways
  • Next steps or action items
  • Customer satisfaction indicators
Extracted variables are stored in gathered_context and available in webhooks, reports, and the Run Detail page.

Multiple End Call Nodes

Use different End Call nodes connected via labeled edges to create distinct closing paths:

  • Happy path: Lead qualified → "Great, we'll send you the proposal today!"
  • Not interested: No interest detected → "Thank you for your time, have a great day!"
  • Voicemail: Voicemail detected → Leave a brief message
Each Edge can carry a condition and a transition_speech that the agent says as it transitions to that ending.

End Call Tool vs. End Call Node

  • End Call Node: A workflow graph node — reached via edges, executes a closing prompt, extracts data, then hangs up
  • End Call Tool: A tool the LLM can invoke at any point during a call — useful for conditional termination (e.g., caller explicitly asks to end, timeout reached)
See End Call Tool for the tool variant.

documents.title: Agent Node
documents.excerpt: The core conversational building block — each Agent node runs one focused LLM exchange with tools, documents, and variable extraction.
documents.content:
The Agent Node is the core conversational unit in a Verasist workflow. Each Agent node represents one focused step in the conversation where the LLM engages with the caller, can invoke tools, reference documents, and extract structured data.

Most workflows are a chain of Agent nodes connected by edges that describe transition conditions. For example: Greet → Qualify → Handle Objection → Present Offer → Close.

Configuration

Name

A short identifier for this step (e.g., "Qualify Budget", "Gather Preferences"). Appears in call logs and edge transition labels.

Prompt

The system prompt for this conversational step. This is the core instruction the LLM follows during this node. 
Ask the caller about their budget range and timeline. If they mention a number, confirm it. Once you have both budget and timeline, transition to the next step.

Supports {{template_variables}} from:

  • Pre-call fetch responses
  • Variables extracted in previous nodes
  • Default context (caller number, time, date)

Allow Interruption

When enabled, the caller can interrupt the agent mid-utterance. Turn this off for steps where the agent must deliver a complete message (e.g., legal disclaimers, pricing details).

Add Global Prompt

When enabled and a Global node exists, the global persona/tone instructions are prepended to this node's prompt at runtime.

Extraction

When enabled, the LLM runs a structured extraction pass after the turn completes:
  • Extraction Prompt: Overall instructions for what to extract
  • Extraction Variables: Named variables with types (string, number, boolean) and per-variable hints
{
  "name": "budget_usd",
  "type": "number",
  "prompt": "Stated budget in USD, or 0 if not mentioned"
}

Extracted variables flow into gathered_context and are available in subsequent nodes via {{gathered_context.budget_usd}}.

Tools

Select tools the agent can invoke during this step. The LLM decides when to invoke each tool based on the conversation context. Fewer tools per node means more reliable tool invocation.

Documents

Select knowledge base documents the agent can reference. The retrieval mode (Full Document or Chunked Search) depends on your knowledge base configuration.

Edges & Transitions

Edges connected to an Agent node define where the conversation goes next. Each edge has:

  • Target Node: The next node in the workflow
  • Condition: A natural-language description of when to take this path (e.g., "Caller shows interest", "Caller declines")
  • Label: A short label shown on the canvas
  • Transition Speech: Optional phrase the agent says before leaving this node (e.g., "Great, let me check our availability for you!")
The LLM evaluates all outgoing edges and picks the most appropriate one based on the conversation.

Best Practices

  • One goal per node: Each Agent node should have a single, clear objective
  • Keep prompts short: 3–5 sentences is usually enough; the Global node handles shared instructions
  • Extract early: Capture structured data as soon as the caller provides it
  • Limit tools per node: Attach only the tools relevant to this step's objective
  • Use transition speech: Brief bridging phrases make the conversation feel natural

documents.title: Global Node
documents.excerpt: Define shared persona, tone, and rules that apply across your entire workflow — appended to every node's prompt at runtime.
documents.content:
You should have only one Global node per Voice Agent. It has no incoming or outgoing edges.

The Global node defines instructions that are automatically appended to the system prompt of every node where Add Global Prompt is enabled. Use it for shared concerns that apply across the entire conversation.

Configuration

Name

A short identifier shown on the canvas (e.g., "Persona & Tone"). Has no runtime effect.

Global Prompt

The text appended to every prompted node's system prompt. Supports {{template_variables}}.

Default: 

You are a helpful assistant whose mode of interaction with the user is voice.
So don't use any special characters which can not be pronounced.
Use short sentences and simple language.

What to Put in the Global Node

| Concern | Example | |---------|---------| | Persona | "You are Sarah, a warm and professional representative from Acme Corp." | | Tone | "Always speak in short, conversational sentences. Be empathetic but efficient." | | Compliance | "Never make promises about pricing or delivery dates. Escalate legal questions." | | Objection Handling | "If the caller objects to pricing, acknowledge their concern before responding." | | Company Facts | "Our headquarters is in San Francisco. We've been in business since 2019." | | Language Rules | "Always respond in the same language the caller uses." |

Per-Node Control

Each node has an Add Global Prompt toggle:

  • On (default for Agent nodes): The global prompt is prepended to the node's prompt
  • Off: The node runs with only its own prompt — useful for closing messages or nodes with very specific instructions

Best Practices

  • Keep the global prompt under 500 words to avoid crowding per-node prompts
  • Use per-node prompts for step-specific instructions; use the global node only for shared concerns
  • Turn off Add Global Prompt on End Call nodes if you want a clean closing message without persona instructions

documents.title: QA
documents.excerpt: Define post-call quality analysis criteria that automatically evaluate agent performance, compliance, and conversation quality after each run.
documents.content:
The QA node lets you define quality analysis criteria that are automatically evaluated after each call ends. Use it to score agent performance, check compliance, or extract structured insights from conversations.

How It Works

  1. Define Criteria: Create QA criteria in the node — each is a question or scoring rubric
  2. Automatic Evaluation: After each call, the LLM evaluates the conversation transcript against all criteria
  3. View Results: Scores appear on the Run Detail page for each individual run

Creating a QA Node

Add a QA node to your workflow from the Voice Agent Builder. Configure each analysis criterion with:

  • Name: Short identifier (e.g., "Greeting Quality", "Compliance Check")
  • Description: What to evaluate and how to score it
  • Scale: Score range (e.g., 1–5, pass/fail)

Example QA Criteria

| Criterion | Description | Scale | |-----------|-------------|-------| | Greeting Quality | Did the agent introduce themselves and state the company name? | 1–5 | | Compliance | Did the agent avoid making unauthorized promises or guarantees? | Pass/Fail | | Empathy | Did the agent acknowledge the caller's emotions appropriately? | 1–5 | | Call Resolution | Was the caller's issue fully resolved by the end of the call? | Yes/No | | Objection Handling | Did the agent address objections without being defensive? | 1–5 |

Viewing QA Results

After a call completes, the QA analysis runs automatically. Results are available on the Run Detail page, showing:

  • Individual scores for each criterion
  • Overall quality score
  • LLM-generated feedback explaining each score
Use these scores to monitor agent performance trends, identify training gaps, and improve your prompts over time.

documents.title: API Trigger
documents.excerpt: Trigger outbound calls from external systems like n8n, Zapier, or your own backend
documents.content:
The API Trigger node lets you initiate outbound calls to your voice agent programmatically. When you add an API Trigger node to your workflow, Verasist generates a unique endpoint URL that external systems can call to start a conversation.

This is useful when you want to trigger calls from your own backend, a CRM, or workflow tools like n8n and Zapier.

Prerequisites

  • A configured telephony provider — outbound calls will fail without one
  • An API key for authentication

Finding your trigger URL

When you add an API Trigger node to your workflow, Verasist assigns it a unique UUID. The trigger node exposes two URLs that share this UUID:

  • A production URL for the published workflow
  • A test URL for the latest draft
You can copy either URL from the trigger node's settings dialog. 
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid}        # Production
POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid}   # Test

If you are using the hosted version, replace verasist.ai with api.verasist.ai.

Test vs production

| Mode | URL | Runs | |------------|------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Production | /api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} | The published version of the agent. | | Test | /api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} | The latest draft. Falls back to the published version if no draft exists. |

Use the test URL while iterating on changes so production traffic continues to hit the published version.

The production URL only executes a published workflow. If you update the workflow but do not publish it, the production trigger will continue to run the older published version.

Once you publish your draft, both URLs run the same definition.

A common pitfall is editing the workflow, saving the draft, and then calling the production trigger URL expecting the new behavior. That will not work until you publish the workflow. Use the test URL to verify draft changes before publishing.

The request body, headers, and response shape are identical for both URLs.

Channels

By default, an API Trigger node launches a phone call, but the node can be configured for a different channel — whatsapp, telegram, instagram, or text — and a request can override that channel per call by passing channel in the request body.

| channel | Required request fields | Response message | |---|---|---| | phone (default) | phone_number | null | | whatsapp / telegram / instagram | target (destination identity for that channel), channel_configuration_id (unless the node has one configured) | The workflow's first generated reply | | text | — | The workflow's first generated reply |

text starts the workflow without any external channel — the response body itself contains the agent's first message, useful for embedding the agent in your own UI without setting up a channel integration.

``bash WhatsApp channel curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "channel": "whatsapp", "target": "+14155550100", "channel_configuration_id": 12, "initial_context": {"customer_name": "Jane"} }' 


channel is required in the request body when neither the node nor the request otherwise specify one — for example when triggering by workflow UUID directly, which has no node to fall back to.


Making a request


Authenticate by passing your API key in the X-API-Key header. For the default phone channel, the request body requires a phone_number and accepts optional initial_context and telephony_configuration_id fields (see Channels above for the fields required by other channels).
bash Production URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }'
bash Test URL curl -X POST https://verasist.ai/api/v1/public/agent/test/{uuid} \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "X-API-Key: vrs_your_api_key" \ -d '{ "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "customer_name": "Jane", "appointment_date": "March 15" } }' 


Use the test URL when you want to verify draft changes before publishing.


Response


A successful request returns a workflow_run_id that you can use to retrieve run details, recordings, and transcripts.
json { "status": "initiated", "workflow_run_id": 12345, "workflow_run_name": "WR-API-7823" } 


Error responses


| Status | Cause |
|---|---|
| 400 | Telephony provider not configured, or call failed to initiate |
| 401 | Missing or invalid API key |
| 403 | API key does not have access to this agent |
| 404 | Trigger not found or not active |


Initial context

initial_context is a JSON object containing any information you want your voice agent to access during the call. You can reference these values in your prompts using template variables — values enclosed in {{ and }}.

For example, if your request includes:
json { "phone_number": "+14155550100", "initial_context": { "user": { "name": "John" } } } 

You can reference the user's name in your agent prompt as {{user.name}} — in Agent prompts, initial_context fields are referenced directly by name (not prefixed with initial_context.). See template variables for the exact syntax in prompts versus webhook payloads.


See Context & Variables for more on how data flows through a call.


Choosing a telephony configuration


By default, calls are placed through your organization's default outbound telephony configuration. To route a specific call through a different configuration — for example, to dial out from a regional number — pass telephony_configuration_id in the request body.
json { "phone_number": "+14155550100", "telephony_configuration_id": 42 } `

The id is shown on each row in Telephony configurations (https://app.verasist.ai/telephony-configurations for hosted or http://localhost:3010/telephony-configurations for local). The configuration must belong to the same organization as the API Trigger; otherwise the request returns 404`.

For full endpoint details including all parameters and response fields, see the API reference.

documents.title: Webhook
documents.excerpt: Webhook node allow you to sync the result of Voice Agent runs to your external systems, like CRM or to other workflow orchestrator like Zapier or n8n.
documents.content:
Video Tutorial

You can have multiple Webhook Nodes for a single Voice Agent, if you want to sync the result of the call at multiple places.

The Webhook node sends an HTTP request to an external system after the workflow completes.

Configuration

| Field | Description | |---|---| | enabled | When off, the webhook is skipped at run time. | | http_method | The HTTP verb for the outbound request: GET, POST (default), PUT, PATCH, or DELETE. | | endpoint_url | The URL the request is sent to. | | credential_uuid | Optional stored credential (API key, bearer token, basic auth, or custom header — configured under Credentials) applied to the request's auth header. | | custom_headers | Optional list of additional HTTP headers to include, e.g. [{"key": "X-Source", "value": "verasist"}]. | | payload_template | The JSON body of the request (see below). Not used for GET/DELETE. |

Creating the Webhook Payload

The payload can contain a valid JSON, and you can reference variables while constructing that payload. You can reference below variables while constructing the payload.
  • {{workflow_run_id}} Unique ID of the Agent run
  • {{workflow_id}} ID of the Agent
  • {{workflow_name}} Name of the workflow
  • {{campaign_id}} ID of the campaign this run belongs to (empty for ad-hoc runs)
  • {{call_time}} ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when the call was initiated
  • {{initial_context.*}} Initial context variables
  • {{gathered_context.*}} Extracted variables
  • {{cost_info.call_duration_seconds}} Call duration
  • {{recording_url}} Call recording URL
  • {{transcript_url}} Transcript URL
For the full list of available variables, authentication options, and receiver examples, see the Webhook Payloads developer reference.

An example of the payload is given below

{
  "call_id": "{{workflow_run_id}}",
  "first_name": "{{initial_context.first_name}}",
  "rsvp": "{{gathered_context.rsvp}}",
  "duration": "{{cost_info.call_duration_seconds}}",
  "recording_url": "{{recording_url}}",
  "transcript_url": "{{transcript_url}}"
}

documents.title: Add to Website
documents.excerpt: Add your Verasist voice agent to any website so visitors can talk to it.
documents.content:
How to add it

Add your voice agent to any website using the Configure Widget dialog in your agent's settings.

Step 1: Open the agent settings by clicking the gear icon in the top-right of the agent editor.

Step 2: Scroll to the Add to Website section and click Configure Widget.

Step 3: Enable embedding, add your website's domain to Allowed Domains, choose Floating Widget, Inline Component, or Headless (Bring Your Own UI), customize the button (position, color, text) if applicable, and click Save Configurations.

Step 4: Copy the generated embed code and paste it into your web page to test your agent.

Embed modes

| Mode | What it renders | When to use | | --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Floating Widget | A pill-shaped CTA button anchored to a corner of the page. | You want a turn-key chat-bubble experience that doesn't disturb your existing layout. | | Inline Component | A panel rendered inside a

that you place in your page. | You want the agent embedded in a specific section (landing-page hero, support tab, etc.). | | Headless | No UI. Only the audio pipeline plus a JavaScript API on window.VerasistWidget. | You want full control over the UI — your own buttons, design system, framework state, animations. |

Prerequisites

These apply to all three modes:

  • Serve your page over HTTPS or from http://localhost. Browsers refuse microphone access on plain HTTP origins or file://.
  • If you set Allowed Domains in the dashboard, include your test origin (e.g. localhost) — otherwise the widget's config and signaling requests are rejected. Leave the list empty to allow all domains.
  • The embed snippet you copy from the dashboard is a single

    React + TypeScript

    import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';

    type CallStatus = 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'connected' | 'failed';
    

    declare global {
  interface Window {
    VerasistWidget: {
      start: () => void;
      end: () => void;
      onStatusChange: (cb: (status: CallStatus, text?: string, subtext?: string) => void) => void;
      onError: (cb: (err: Error) => void) => void;
    };
  }
}
    

    export function TalkButton() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('idle');
    

    useEffect(() => {
    window.VerasistWidget.onStatusChange((s) => setStatus(s));
    window.VerasistWidget.onError((err) => console.error('Verasist error:', err.message));
  }, []);
    

    const isLive = status === 'connected' || status === 'connecting';
  const label = { idle: 'Talk to AI', connecting: 'Connecting…', connected: 'End Call', failed: 'Retry' }[status];
    

    return (
    
  );
}

    start() must run inside a real user-gesture handler (click, touchend, etc.). Browsers refuse to grant microphone access to scripts that request it outside of one — calling start() from a setTimeout or on page load will fail with a permission error.

    Lifecycle callbacks (all modes)

    The on* callbacks in the Headless JavaScript API work in all three embed modes, not just Headless. Use them for analytics or to trigger UI in the host page even when the widget is rendering its own UI (Floating or Inline).

    window.VerasistWidget.onCallConnected(({ agentId, workflowRunId }) => {
  analytics.track('voice_call_started', { agentId, workflowRunId });
});

    window.VerasistWidget.onCallDisconnected(({ workflowRunId, durationSeconds }) => {
  analytics.track('voice_call_ended', { workflowRunId, durationSeconds });
});

    onCallConnected and onCallDisconnected only fire when the call actually establishes a media connection — failed-to-connect attempts (e.g. denied mic, network failure) don't trigger them, so analytics stay clean.

documents.title: Telephony Integration
documents.excerpt: Connect voice agents with telephony providers for inbound and outbound calls
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI's telephony integration system provides a unified interface for connecting with various telephony providers. The same configuration powers both outbound calls (initiated from Verasist) and inbound calls (received on a phone number you own).

Supported Providers

Industry-leading cloud communications platform with global reach High-quality voice with 16kHz audio and excellent international coverage Cloud communications platform with programmable voice and global PSTN reach SIP-based telephony with flexible trunk configuration Cloud-based telephony with global reach and competitive pricing Connect an external SIP trunk (NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, etc.) through built-in Asterisk Build your own telephony provider integration

Configuration

All telephony providers are configured from a single page in Verasist:

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select your provider
  3. Enter your credentials and save
  4. Open the new configuration and add at least one phone number
  5. (Optional) Assign an Inbound workflow to a phone number to enable inbound calling

A single org can hold multiple configurations (for example, separate Twilio sub-accounts) and multiple phone numbers per configuration. Mark one configuration as the default outbound to use it for test calls and campaigns by default.

Common Features

The telephony integration in Verasist AI supports:

  • Outbound Calls: Initiate calls to any phone number from a workflow or campaign
  • Inbound Calls: Route incoming calls to the right voice agent — see the Inbound Calling guide
  • Call Transfer: Transfer an in-progress call to a human or another number (provider-dependent)
  • Call Status Tracking: Monitor call lifecycle events (initiated, ringing, answered, completed, failed)
  • WebSocket Audio Streaming: Real-time, bidirectional audio between caller and agent
  • Webhook Signature Verification: Inbound webhooks are verified against the matched configuration's credentials

Inbound Calling

Inbound calls use a single org-wide webhook URL:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run

Verasist resolves the org from the webhook's account credentials and the agent from the called number's Inbound workflow assignment. See Inbound Calling for the full setup.

Troubleshooting

Calls not connecting- Verify credentials are correctly configured - Check phone number format (E.164 with country code, e.g. +1234567890) - Ensure webhook URLs are publicly accessible - Review provider-specific error logs
Audio quality issues- Check network bandwidth and latency - Verify audio codec compatibility - Review WebSocket connection stability
Webhook signature validation failing- Confirm auth tokens / API secrets match between provider and Verasist configuration - Verify webhook URL matches exactly (including the /inbound/run path) - Check for proxy or load balancer modifications

Next Steps

  • Set up your first telephony provider
  • Configure inbound calling
  • Build a custom provider integration

documents.title: Inbound Calling
documents.excerpt: Configure inbound calling for Twilio, Vonage, Plivo, Telnyx, Cloudonix, Vobiz, and SIP Trunk providers in Verasist AI
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI supports inbound calling across all supported telephony providers. When someone calls your configured phone number, your voice agent automatically answers and handles the interaction. Inbound and outbound calls share the same telephony configuration.

Supported Providers for Inbound Calls

Industry-leading platform with robust inbound call handling Application-level inbound routing with high-quality 16kHz audio Application-level inbound routing on Plivo's global voice cloud Application-level inbound via Telnyx Call Control API SIP-based inbound calling with flexible trunk configuration Cloud-based telephony with global reach and competitive pricing Bring your own SIP trunk from NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, or any standards-compliant provider

How Inbound Calling Works

Verasist exposes a single inbound webhook URL for the whole org:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run

When a call arrives:

  1. Call Received: Your telephony provider receives the incoming call
  2. Webhook Triggered: The provider sends a webhook to /inbound/run
  3. Org & Agent Resolved: Verasist identifies the org from the webhook's account credentials, then looks up which agent should answer based on the called number's Inbound workflow assignment in your telephony configuration
  4. Audio Streaming: Real-time audio streams between caller and agent via WebSocket
  5. Conversation Handled: Your voice agent manages the entire conversation
You don't construct per-workflow URLs anymore — the routing is done by the called number's inbound workflow assignment in Verasist.

Configuration in Verasist AI

Setting up inbound calling takes three steps:

Step 1: Configure Telephony Provider

The telephony configuration for inbound calling is identical to outbound calling. Add (or open) a configuration at /telephony-configurations following your provider's documentation:

  • Twilio Configuration
  • Vonage Configuration
  • Plivo Configuration
  • Telnyx Configuration
  • Cloudonix Configuration
  • Vobiz Configuration
  • SIP Trunk Configuration

Step 2: Assign an Inbound Workflow to the Phone Number

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save
This is what tells Verasist which agent to run when a call comes in for that number.

Step 3: Point Your Provider at /inbound/run

Each provider needs its inbound webhook (Twilio Voice URL / Vonage Answer URL / etc.) set to the global Verasist endpoint:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run
If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain.

The exact place to set this varies by provider — follow the provider-specific instructions:

  • Twilio Inbound Setup
  • Vonage Inbound Setup
  • Plivo Inbound Setup
  • Telnyx Inbound Setup
  • Cloudonix Inbound Setup
  • Vobiz Inbound Setup
  • SIP Trunk Inbound Setup

Testing Inbound Calls

After completing both the Verasist AI configuration and provider-specific setup:

  1. Test Call: Call your configured phone number from another phone
  2. Verify Connection: Ensure your voice agent answers and responds appropriately
