Verasist pushed this URL automatically when you saved the inbound workflow in Step 2. The same URL is shared across every number linked to that application — Verasist routes each inbound call to the right agent based on the called number's inbound workflow assignment. If the field is empty, shows a different URL, or Verasist surfaced a sync warning on save, the auto-push failed — most often because the Auth ID/Token or Application ID in Verasist is incorrect. Paste the URL into the field yourself, set the method to POST, and save. On self-hosted Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your backend domain.

Step 4: Verify Setup

  • Ensure your Verasist AI instance is publicly accessible
  • Verify any firewalls allow Vobiz's webhook requests

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured Vobiz phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI voice agent answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in both Verasist AI dashboard and Vobiz dashboard

Troubleshooting

Invalid phone number errorEnsure phone numbers include country code in E.164 format: +1234567890
Authentication failed- Verify Auth ID and Auth Token are correct - Check for extra spaces in credentials - Ensure credentials haven't been regenerated in Vobiz dashboard
Webhook requests failing- Confirm your Auth Token matches exactly - Verify the webhook URL is accessible from Vobiz servers - Check if you're behind a proxy that modifies requests
No audio on calls- Verify WebSocket connection is established - Check firewall rules for WebSocket traffic - Ensure audio pipeline is configured correctly
Inbound calls go to voicemail or aren't answered- Verify the phone number is linked to the same Vobiz Application whose ID you configured in Verasist - Confirm the called number exists in your Verasist telephony configuration and has an Inbound workflow assigned - After assigning the inbound workflow, confirm Verasist successfully updated the application's answer_url (no warning shown on save) - Verify Verasist AI instance is running and responding
Voice agent doesn't respond to inbound calls- Confirm the phone number has an Inbound workflow assigned in /telephony-configurations - Check webhook signature validation is working (Auth Token in Verasist matches Vobiz dashboard) - Verify WebSocket connection establishes successfully - Review call logs for error messages

Best Practices

  • Test your configuration with a single call before running campaigns
  • Monitor Vobiz dashboard for usage and billing
  • Keep your Auth Token secure and rotate it periodically
  • Use a dedicated Vobiz Application for Verasist so the shared answer_url doesn't conflict with other systems

documents.title: SIP Trunk Integration
documents.excerpt: Connect your SIP trunk provider (NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, Flowroute, etc.) for voice communication in Verasist AI
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI supports external SIP trunk providers through its built-in Asterisk PJSIP stack. When you configure a SIP trunk, Verasist handles all call control (origination, bridging, teardown) automatically — you only need to provide your provider's SIP credentials.

Supported SIP trunk providers include: NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, Flowroute, Vobiz, and any standards-compliant SIP trunk provider.

Prerequisites

  • An active SIP trunk from a supported provider (NetGSM, Verimor, Twilio Elastic SIP, Flowroute, Vobiz, etc.)
  • SIP credentials from your provider:
- Gateway IP / Hostname — The provider's SIP server address - Username & Password — SIP authentication credentials - From User / Caller ID (optional) — The number or user shown on outbound calls - DID Numbers — The phone numbers assigned to your trunk
  • Your provider must allow traffic from the Verasist server IP (see Firewall & IP Whitelisting)

Configuration

Step 1: Obtain SIP Trunk Credentials

  1. Sign up with your SIP trunk provider (NetGSM, Verimor, etc.)
  2. Obtain from your provider:
- Gateway IP / Hostname — The provider's SIP server address (e.g. sip.netgsm.com.tr) - Username & Password — SIP authentication credentials - From User / Caller ID (optional) — The caller identity for outbound calls. Defaults to username if not set. - DID Numbers — The phone numbers assigned to your trunk
  1. Note whether your provider requires SIP registration (register: true) or uses IP-based authentication (register: false). Most providers (NetGSM, Verimor) require registration.

Step 2: IP Whitelisting (Kritik Önemli)

Most SIP trunk providers (NetGSM, Verimor, etc.) require you to whitelist the server IP that will send/receive SIP traffic. This is a security measure — without it, your provider will reject SIP registration and inbound/outbound calls will fail.

Yapmanız gerekenler:

  1. Verasist sunucunuzun public IP adresini öğrenin
  2. SIP trunk sağlayıcınızın yönetim paneline giriş yapın:
- NetGSM: "Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama" veya "Güvenlik" menüsünden IP ekleyin - Verimor: Müşteri panelinden IP whitelist bölümüne gidin - Diğer sağlayıcılar: İlgili güvenlik / firewall / allowed IPs ayarlarını bulun
  1. Verasist sunucunuzun public IP'sini listeye ekleyin
  2. Değişikliğin yayılmasını bekleyin (genellikle anında, bazen birkaç dakika)

Step 3: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /telephony-configurations and click Add configuration
  2. Select SIP Trunk (Asterisk) as your provider
| Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | Gateway IP | SIP provider's gateway IP or hostname (required). Örn: sip.netgsm.com.tr | | Gateway Port | SIP port, usually 5060 (default: 5060) | | Username | SIP authentication username (required) | | Password | SIP authentication password (required) | | From User | Caller identity for outbound INVITE (defaults to username) | | Register | Enable outbound SIP registration (default: enabled). NetGSM, Verimor gibi çoğu sağlayıcı için true olmalıdır. | | From Numbers | Phone numbers / DIDs for outbound caller ID | | ARI Endpoint | Internal Asterisk ARI URL (auto-filled from server config) | | App Name | Stasis application name (auto-filled from server config) | | App Password | ARI user password (auto-filled from server config) |
The ARI Endpoint, App Name, and App Password fields are pre-filled from the server environment (ASTERISK_ARI_ENDPOINT, ASTERISK_ARI_USERNAME, ASTERISK_ARI_PASSWORD). You only need to fill in the SIP trunk provider credentials (Gateway IP, Username, Password).
  1. Click Save Configuration
  2. Open the configuration you just created and add at least one phone number (with country code in E.164 format, e.g. +905321234567)

Step 4: Test Your Configuration

  1. Create a test workflow
  2. Click "Call" to verify outbound connectivity
  3. Check call logs for successful connection

Firewall & IP Whitelisting

When using a SIP Trunk provider, you must whitelist the Verasist server's public IP address on your provider's side. This is critical because:

  • SIP signaling (port 5060) and RTP media (port range 10000-20000) traffic originates from the Verasist server
  • Most providers reject traffic from unknown IPs for security reasons
  • If your Verasist instance IP changes, you must update the whitelist with your provider
Steps:
  1. Find your Verasist server's public IP address
  2. Log in to your SIP trunk provider's dashboard (e.g. NetGSM's management panel)
  3. Navigate to security / IP whitelist / allowed IPs settings
  4. Add your Verasist server's public IP
  5. Wait for the change to propagate (usually instant, but can take a few minutes)

Inbound Calling Setup

Inbound calls use the same org-wide webhook URL as other telephony providers:

https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/telephony/inbound/run
If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain.

DID Routing

Your SIP trunk provider must route incoming calls to the Verasist server. The setup varies by provider:

  1. DID Routing: In your provider's dashboard, configure each DID/phone number to forward incoming calls to the Verasist server's IP address. Some providers call this "DID forwarding", "call routing", or "destination configuration".
  2. SIP Registration: If your trunk uses registration (register: true), incoming calls are automatically routed to the registered endpoint. No additional DID routing is needed.
  3. IP Authentication: If your trunk uses IP-based auth (register: false), make sure the provider knows to send calls to your Verasist server IP.

Assign an Inbound Workflow

  1. Go to /telephony-configurations and open your configuration
  2. In the Phone numbers section, edit the number that should receive inbound calls
  3. Set its Inbound workflow to the agent that should answer
  4. Save

Test Inbound Calling

  1. Call your configured phone number from another phone
  2. Verify your Verasist AI voice agent answers and responds
  3. Check call logs in the Verasist dashboard

Provider-Specific Notes

NetGSM

NetGSM is a Turkish SIP trunk provider. Key setup details:

  • IP Whitelisting: After obtaining your trunk credentials, log in to the NetGSM customer panel and add the Verasist server IP to the allowed IP list (usually found under "Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama" or similar)
  • DID Routing: Configure each DID to forward to the Verasist server IP under "Santral" → "Yönlendirme"
  • Registration: NetGSM requires SIP registration (register: true)
  • Gateway: The gateway address (e.g. sip.netgsm.com.tr) is provided in your NetGSM welcome email
  • Codec: NetGSM supports G.711 (alaw/ulaw)

Verimor

Verimor is a Turkish SIP trunk and call management provider. Key setup details:

  • IP Whitelisting: Add the Verasist server IP to Verimor's allowed IP list through the customer panel
  • Registration: Verimor requires SIP registration (register: true)
  • Gateway: The gateway address is provided in your Verimor account details
  • DID Routing: Configure DID forwarding to the Verasist server IP in the Verimor panel

Twilio Elastic SIP Trunking

  • Create an Elastic SIP Trunk in the Twilio console
  • Configure the trunk's termination URI to point to the Verasist server IP
  • Twilio uses IP-based authentication by default — make sure your trunk's "Authentication" is configured correctly
  • Set register: false in Verasist for IP-based auth

Other Providers

For Flowroute, Vobiz, or any other SIP trunk provider, the process is similar:

  1. Obtain SIP credentials from the provider
  2. Whitelist the Verasist server IP on the provider's side
  3. Configure DID routing for inbound calls
  4. Enter the gateway IP/username/password in Verasist's SIP configuration

Troubleshooting

SIP registration failing- Verify the gateway IP and port are correct - Check that the Verasist server IP is whitelisted by your SIP provider - Confirm username and password match the provider's credentials - Ensure the provider's gateway is reachable from the Verasist server (try ping or telnet gateway_ip 5060)
Inbound calls not reaching Verasist- Check DID routing configuration in your provider's panel — calls must be directed to the Verasist server IP - Ensure IP whitelisting is configured correctly - Verify the phone number is added to your Verasist configuration with an inbound workflow assigned
Outbound calls not connecting- Verify the DID/from number is added to the configuration - Check that the provider's gateway is reachable - Review Asterisk logs for detailed SIP error messages
Audio issues- Ensure RTP ports (10000-20000) are not blocked by a firewall - Check codec compatibility with your provider (G.711 is widely supported) - Verify network latency between Verasist and the SIP provider
  1. Obtain gateway IP, username, and password from your provider
  2. Whitelist the Verasist server IP on the provider's side
  3. Configure DID routing to the Verasist server
  4. Enter credentials in Verasist's SIP Trunk configuration

Troubleshooting

SIP registration failing- Verify the gateway IP and port are correct - Check that the Verasist server IP is whitelisted by your SIP provider - Confirm username and password match the provider's credentials - Ensure the provider's gateway is reachable from the Verasist server (try ping or telnet gateway_ip 5060)
Inbound calls not reaching Verasist- Check DID routing configuration in your provider's panel — calls must be directed to the Verasist server IP - Ensure IP whitelisting is configured correctly - Verify the phone number is added to your Verasist configuration with an inbound workflow assigned
Outbound calls not connecting- Verify the DID/from number is added to the configuration - Check that the provider's gateway is reachable - Review Asterisk logs for detailed SIP error messages
Audio issues- Ensure RTP ports (10000-20000) are not blocked by a firewall - Check codec compatibility with your provider (G.711 is widely supported) - Verify network latency between Verasist and the SIP provider
NetGSM specific issues- Confirm IP whitelisting is complete in the NetGSM panel ("Ayarlar" → "IP Kısıtlama") - Verify DID routing (Yönlendirme) is pointing to the Verasist server IP - Check that each DID is properly assigned in NetGSM - Contact NetGSM support if your trunk status shows "Kayıtsız" (unregistered)

documents.title: Webhooks and Callbacks
documents.excerpt: How Verasist handles telephony webhooks for call events, audio streaming, and status updates across providers.
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist uses webhooks to communicate with telephony providers for call events and audio streaming. Webhooks are automatically configured when you set up a telephony integration.

Webhook Types

1. Initial Call Webhook

When a call is initiated, the telephony provider requests instructions from Verasist.

Endpoint: Provider-specific — varies by provider and is auto-configured during setup.

Purpose: Returns provider-specific instructions (TwiML, NCCO, etc.) that tell the provider how to handle the call.

Twilio (TwiML)

Vonage (NCCO)

    [
      {
        "action": "connect",
        "endpoint": [{
          "type": "websocket",
          "uri": "wss://your-domain/api/v1/telephony/ws/123/456/789",
          "content-type": "audio/l16;rate=16000"
        }]
      }
    ]

Plivo (XML)

2. Status Callback

Receives call lifecycle events from the provider (call answered, completed, failed, etc.). These are sent to provider-specific endpoints and used to update the run state in Verasist.

3. Inbound Call Handler

For inbound calls, Verasist provides a dedicated inbound endpoint per workflow:

  • New: POST /api/v1/telephony/inbound/run with telephony configuration context
  • Deprecated: POST /api/v1/telephony/inbound/{workflow_id}
The inbound endpoint receives the call, matches it to the correct workflow, and starts the voice agent.

4. Fallback Handler

POST /api/v1/telephony/inbound/fallback — Used when an inbound call cannot be matched to a specific workflow.

5. Transfer Result Callback

POST /api/v1/telephony/transfer-result/{transfer_id} — Receives the result of a Call Transfer operation (answered, no-answer, busy, failed).

WebSocket Audio Streaming

Verasist uses WebSocket connections for real-time audio streaming between the provider and the AI agent:

| Endpoint | Use | |----------|-----| | /api/v1/telephony/ws/{workflow_id}/{user_id}/{workflow_run_id} | Standard telephony WebSocket | | /api/v1/telephony/ws/ari | Asterisk ARI WebSocket | | /api/v1/agent-stream/{workflow_uuid} | Provider-agnostic external streaming |

These endpoints are automatically configured during call setup — no manual configuration is needed.

Endpoint: /api/v1/telephony/status-callback/{workflow_run_id}

Events Tracked:

  • initiated - Call request received
  • ringing - Call is ringing
  • answered - Call was answered
  • completed - Call ended normally
  • busy - Line was busy
  • no-answer - Call not answered
  • failed - Call failed

3. WebSocket Audio Stream

Real-time audio streaming for voice interaction.

Endpoint: /api/v1/telephony/ws/{workflow_id}/{user_id}/{workflow_run_id}

Audio Formats:

  • Twilio: 8kHz μ-law (MULAW), Base64-encoded in JSON messages
  • Vonage: 16kHz Linear PCM, Binary frames

How It Works

Verasist AI automatically:

  1. Constructs webhook URLs based on your deployment
  2. Passes them to the telephony provider when initiating calls
  3. Verifies webhook signatures for security:
- Twilio: HMAC-SHA1 signature validation - Vonage: JWT token verification
  1. Processes status updates to track call lifecycle
  2. Manages WebSocket connections for audio streaming
  3. Handles provider-specific audio formats and protocols

Local Development

For local development, use the built-in Cloudflare tunnel:

# docker-compose.yml includes:
cloudflared:
  image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
  command: tunnel --no-autoupdate --url http://api:8000

The tunnel URL is automatically detected and used for webhooks.

Troubleshooting

Webhook URL not accessible- Verify your domain/tunnel URL is publicly accessible - Check firewall rules allow incoming HTTPS traffic - Test with curl from external network
WebSocket connection dropping- Check WebSocket upgrade headers are preserved - Verify no timeout on load balancer/proxy - Monitor for memory/CPU constraints
Status callbacks not received- Verify workflow_run_id is included in URL - Check provider console for webhook errors - Review webhook retry logs

documents.title: Agent Stream
documents.excerpt: Stream audio to a Verasist agent over a WebSocket
documents.content:
Overview

Agent Stream is a WebSocket endpoint that lets a telephony provider point its media stream at a single URL and drive a Verasist agent run. The agent UUID in the URL selects the agent; provider-specific identifiers in the query string (for Cloudonix: Domain) tell Verasist which stored telephony configuration to use for that call. The bearer token and other credentials are never passed in the URL — they live in the stored configuration and are used by Verasist to validate the session and to issue provider API calls (hangup, transfer) during the call.

This is useful when:

  • You're integrating Verasist into a SIP gateway or in-house dialer that already speaks a supported provider's streaming protocol
  • You want one stable endpoint per agent rather than wiring up an inbound webhook per phone number
Agent Stream currently supports the Cloudonix provider only. Other providers return NotImplementedError until a per-provider implementation lands. If you need Twilio, Plivo, Telnyx, Vonage, ARI, or another provider, please open a request on GitHub Discussions with your use case.

Endpoint

wss://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/agent-stream/{agent_uuid}

{agent_uuid} is the agent's stable UUID (see Get the Agent UUID below). On self-hosted deployments, replace app.verasist.ai with your backend host.

Prerequisites

  • A Verasist agent (workflow) — published or in draft is fine
  • A Cloudonix telephony configuration in your Verasist organization whose domain_id matches the Domain you pass on the URL. Verasist uses the bearer token from this configuration to validate the call session and to issue provider API calls (hangup, transfer).

Get the Agent UUID

The Agent UUID is the workflow's stable identifier — it doesn't change when versions are published.

To find and copy it in the UI, see Agent UUID.

Connect to the WebSocket

URL parameters

| Param | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | provider | Yes | Provider name. Currently only cloudonix is supported. | | Domain | Yes (cloudonix) | Cloudonix domain ID. Verasist uses this to look up the matching stored telephony configuration and retrieve the bearer token used for provider API calls. | | callId / CallSid | No | Call identifier from your side; persisted on the workflow run's gathered_context as call_id. The Cloudonix call SID used for streaming is taken from the start event payload, not this param. | | from | No | Caller phone number, persisted on the workflow run as caller_number. | | to | No | Called phone number, persisted on the workflow run as called_number. |

Cloudonix example

wss://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/agent-stream/{agent_uuid}
  ?provider=cloudonix
  &Domain={CLOUDONIX_DOMAIN_ID}
  &callId={CALL_ID}
  &from=+15555550100
  &to=+15555550199

Use this URL inside the CXML your Cloudonix Voice Application returns when the call needs to be bridged to the Verasist agent:

The first two messages on the socket should be Cloudonix's standard connected and start events (Twilio-compatible framing). Verasist extracts streamSid and callSid from the start event payload, validates the session against Cloudonix using the bearer token from the stored telephony configuration matched by Domain, and then begins streaming audio.

Workflow run lifecycle

When the WebSocket is accepted, Verasist:

  1. Looks up the workflow by agent_uuid
  2. Runs a quota check against the workflow's owning user
  3. Creates a new WorkflowRun (call_type=inbound, mode=cloudonix, name WR-AGS-XXXXXXXX) with the from/to numbers stamped on initial_context, the callId/CallSid stored as call_id on gathered_context, and Domain recorded under the run's inbound_webhook log
  4. Transitions the run to running and starts the agent pipeline
The run is visible under the agent's Runs tab as soon as it's minted, just like an inbound or outbound call.

Close codes

| Code | Reason | | --- | --- | | 1008 | Routing failure — unknown provider, workflow not found, or quota exceeded | | 1011 | Server-side failure or unsupported provider for Agent Stream | | 4400 | Provider-level handshake error — for cloudonix, missing Domain, no matching telephony configuration, missing bearer token on the configuration, malformed connected/start events, or session validation failed against Cloudonix |

Security notes

  • Treat the URL as a secret — the agent UUID itself authorizes the connection. Store and transmit it only over TLS, and avoid logging the raw URL in places where access is broader than your operations team.
  • No bearer tokens or provider secrets are passed in the URL. Provider credentials live in the stored telephony configuration (matched by Domain for Cloudonix) and are used server-side by Verasist to validate the session and issue provider API calls.

documents.title: Custom Telephony Provider
documents.excerpt: Build your own telephony provider integration for Verasist AI
documents.content:
Overview

A telephony provider is implemented as a self-registering package under api/services/telephony/providers//. The package contributes everything Verasist needs to wire the provider in — the provider class, transport factory, audio config, request/response schemas, optional HTTP routes, and the form metadata used to render its configuration UI — through a single ProviderSpec registered at import time.

Adding a new provider should not require touching the factory, the audio config, the API routes module, the run-pipeline module, or the frontend. The only edits outside the provider folder are:

  1. One import line in api/services/telephony/providers/__init__.py
  2. One import line in api/schemas/telephony_config.py to add the request/response classes to the TelephonyConfigRequest discriminated union

Provider Package Layout

api/services/telephony/providers/your_provider/
├── __init__.py        # Builds and registers ProviderSpec
├── config.py          # Pydantic Request/Response schemas
├── provider.py        # TelephonyProvider subclass
├── transport.py       # Pipecat WebSocket transport factory
├── serializers.py     # Frame serializer (usually re-exports from pipecat)
├── routes.py          # (optional) HTTP webhook/callback handlers
└── strategies.py      # (optional) Transfer/hangup strategies

Three files are required (__init__.py, config.py, provider.py, transport.py). The rest are optional and are discovered automatically when present:

  • routes.py — if the module exists and exports router: APIRouter, the routes module is imported lazily and mounted under /api/v1/telephony by api.routes.telephony via importlib. Providers that only stream over WebSocket (e.g. ARI) can omit it.
  • strategies.py — used by transports that need provider-specific call transfer/hangup logic in the frame serializer (e.g. Twilio Conference transfers).
  • serializers.py — typically a re-export from pipecat. Keep the file even when it's a one-line re-export so transport code imports from .serializers, giving you an obvious place to drop a custom subclass later.

The TelephonyProvider Interface

Subclass TelephonyProvider in provider.py:

from api.services.telephony.base import (
    CallInitiationResult,
    NormalizedInboundData,
    ProviderSyncResult,
    TelephonyProvider,
)

class YourProvider(TelephonyProvider):
    PROVIDER_NAME = "your_provider"
    WEBHOOK_ENDPOINT = "your-provider-xml"  # path under /api/v1/telephony


def __init__(self, config: dict):
        self.api_key = config.get("api_key")
        self.from_numbers = config.get("from_numbers", [])


# ---------- outbound ----------
    async def initiate_call(self, to_number, webhook_url, workflow_run_id=None,
                            from_number=None, **kwargs) -> CallInitiationResult: ...
    async def get_call_status(self, call_id) -> dict: ...
    async def get_call_cost(self, call_id) -> dict: ...
    async def get_available_phone_numbers(self) -> list[str]: ...
    def validate_config(self) -> bool: ...


# ---------- webhooks ----------
    async def verify_webhook_signature(self, url, params, signature) -> bool: ...
    async def get_webhook_response(self, workflow_id, user_id, workflow_run_id) -> str: ...
    def parse_status_callback(self, data: dict) -> dict: ...


# ---------- websocket ----------
    async def handle_websocket(self, websocket, workflow_id, user_id, workflow_run_id): ...


# ---------- inbound ----------
    @classmethod
    def can_handle_webhook(cls, webhook_data, headers) -> bool: ...


@staticmethod
    def parse_inbound_webhook(webhook_data) -> NormalizedInboundData: ...


@staticmethod
    def validate_account_id(config_data, webhook_account_id) -> bool: ...


def normalize_phone_number(self, phone_number: str) -> str: ...


async def verify_inbound_signature(self, url, webhook_data, headers, body="") -> bool: ...


async def start_inbound_stream(self, *, websocket_url, workflow_run_id,
                                   normalized_data, backend_endpoint): ...


@staticmethod
    def generate_error_response(error_type, message) -> tuple: ...


# ---------- transfers ----------
    async def transfer_call(self, destination, transfer_id, conference_name,
                            timeout=30, **kwargs) -> dict: ...
    def supports_transfers(self) -> bool: ...


# ---------- optional ----------
    async def configure_inbound(self, address, webhook_url) -> ProviderSyncResult:
        # Default returns ok=True — implement only if your provider supports
        # programmatic webhook configuration (e.g. binding a number to a URL
        # via API). Used to point inbound numbers at /api/v1/telephony/inbound/run.
        return ProviderSyncResult(ok=True)

See api/services/telephony/base.py for the full docstrings on each method.

Implementation Guide

1. Configuration schemas

Define Pydantic models for the credential payload. The provider Literal discriminator is what makes the schemas dispatch correctly through the registry's discriminated union.

# providers/your_provider/config.py
from typing import List, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class YourProviderConfigurationRequest(BaseModel):
    provider: Literal["your_provider"] = Field(default="your_provider")
    api_key: str = Field(..., description="Your Provider API key")
    api_secret: str = Field(..., description="Your Provider API secret")
    from_numbers: List[str] = Field(default_factory=list)


class YourProviderConfigurationResponse(BaseModel):
    provider: Literal["your_provider"] = Field(default="your_provider")
    api_key: str        # masked when returned
    api_secret: str     # masked when returned
    from_numbers: List[str]

2. Transport factory

Build the Pipecat FastAPIWebsocketTransport for accepted WebSockets. Always load credentials through load_credentials_for_transport so the right config row is picked when the workflow run carries a telephony_configuration_id (multi-config orgs).

# providers/your_provider/transport.py
from fastapi import WebSocket
from api.services.pipecat.audio_config import AudioConfig
from api.services.pipecat.audio_mixer import build_audio_out_mixer
from api.services.telephony.factory import load_credentials_for_transport
from pipecat.transports.websocket.fastapi import (
    FastAPIWebsocketParams,
    FastAPIWebsocketTransport,
)
from .serializers import YourProviderFrameSerializer

async def create_transport(
    websocket: WebSocket,
    workflow_run_id: int,
    audio_config: AudioConfig,
    organization_id: int,
    *,
    vad_config: dict | None = None,
    ambient_noise_config: dict | None = None,
    telephony_configuration_id: int | None = None,
    # provider-specific kwargs (forwarded by run_pipeline_telephony as **transport_kwargs)
    stream_id: str,
    call_id: str,
):
    config = await load_credentials_for_transport(
        organization_id, telephony_configuration_id,
        expected_provider="your_provider",
    )


serializer = YourProviderFrameSerializer(
        stream_id=stream_id,
        call_id=call_id,
        api_key=config["api_key"],
    )
    mixer = await build_audio_out_mixer(
        audio_config.transport_out_sample_rate, ambient_noise_config
    )


return FastAPIWebsocketTransport(
        websocket=websocket,
        params=FastAPIWebsocketParams(
            audio_in_enabled=True,
            audio_out_enabled=True,
            audio_in_sample_rate=audio_config.transport_in_sample_rate,
            audio_out_sample_rate=audio_config.transport_out_sample_rate,
            audio_out_mixer=mixer,
            serializer=serializer,
        ),
    )

3. Routes (optional)

If your provider POSTs webhooks to Verasist (answer URL, status callbacks, hangup callbacks), expose them through a module-level router. The routes are auto-mounted under /api/v1/telephony.

# providers/your_provider/routes.py
from fastapi import APIRouter, Request
from api.services.telephony.status_processor import (
    StatusCallbackRequest,
    _process_status_update,
)

router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/your-provider/status-callback/{workflow_run_id}")
async def status_callback(workflow_run_id: int, request: Request):
    ...

Routes are loaded lazily via importlib from api.routes.telephony._mount_provider_routers, so your route module can freely import other backend services without creating import cycles at provider-class load time.

4. Register the ProviderSpec

The package's __init__.py is where everything comes together:

# providers/your_provider/__init__.py
from typing import Any, Dict

from api.services.pipecat.audio_config import AudioConfig
from api.services.telephony.registry import (
    ProviderSpec,
    ProviderUIField,
    ProviderUIMetadata,
    register,
)


from .config import YourProviderConfigurationRequest, YourProviderConfigurationResponse
from .provider import YourProvider
from .transport import create_transport


def _config_loader(value: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Normalize the stored credentials dict into the constructor shape."""
    return {
        "provider": "your_provider",
        "api_key": value.get("api_key"),
        "api_secret": value.get("api_secret"),
        "from_numbers": value.get("from_numbers", []),
    }


_AUDIO_CONFIG = AudioConfig(
    transport_in_sample_rate=8000,
    transport_out_sample_rate=8000,
    vad_sample_rate=8000,
    pipeline_sample_rate=8000,
    buffer_size_seconds=5.0,
)


_UI_METADATA = ProviderUIMetadata(
    display_name="Your Provider",
    docs_url="https://docs.your-provider.com",
    fields=[
        ProviderUIField(name="api_key",    label="API Key",    type="text",     sensitive=True),
        ProviderUIField(name="api_secret", label="API Secret", type="password", sensitive=True),
        ProviderUIField(
            name="from_numbers", label="Phone Numbers", type="string-array",
            description="E.164-formatted phone numbers used for outbound calls",
        ),
    ],
)


SPEC = ProviderSpec(
    name="your_provider",
    provider_cls=YourProvider,
    config_loader=_config_loader,
    transport_factory=create_transport,
    audio_config=_AUDIO_CONFIG,
    config_request_cls=YourProviderConfigurationRequest,
    config_response_cls=YourProviderConfigurationResponse,
    ui_metadata=_UI_METADATA,
    # Credential field that uniquely identifies the provider account.
    # Used to disambiguate inbound webhooks across multiple configs of the
    # same provider. Empty string for providers without an account-id concept.
    account_id_credential_field="api_key",
)


register(SPEC)

ProviderSpec covers everything downstream code needs:

| Field | Used by | | --- | --- | | name | Stored as the discriminator on every TelephonyConfiguration row and as the WorkflowRunMode value | | provider_cls | factory.get_default_telephony_provider, get_telephony_provider_by_id, get_telephony_provider_for_run | | config_loader | factory._normalize_with_phone_numbers (replaces the old if/elif chain) | | transport_factory | run_pipeline_telephony | | audio_config | create_audio_config() and run_pipeline_telephony | | config_request_cls / config_response_cls | TelephonyConfigRequest discriminated union | | ui_metadata | GET /api/v1/organizations/telephony-providers/metadata (drives the form UI) and the _sensitive_fields masking helper | | account_id_credential_field | Inbound webhook routing across multiple configs of the same provider |

5. Wire the package into the registry import chain

Add one import line to api/services/telephony/providers/__init__.py:

from api.services.telephony.providers import (  # noqa: F401  -- side effects
    ari,
    cloudonix,
    plivo,
    telnyx,
    twilio,
    vobiz,
    vonage,
    your_provider,        # ← add this
)

6. Add to the discriminated union

Add one import block to api/schemas/telephony_config.py so the request/response classes participate in the TelephonyConfigRequest union and the TelephonyConfigurationResponse shape:

from api.services.telephony.providers.your_provider.config import (
    YourProviderConfigurationRequest,
    YourProviderConfigurationResponse,
)

TelephonyConfigRequest = Annotated[
    Union[
        # ...existing entries...
        YourProviderConfigurationRequest,
    ],
    Field(discriminator="provider"),
]


class TelephonyConfigurationResponse(BaseModel):
    # ...existing entries...
    your_provider: Optional[YourProviderConfigurationResponse] = None

That's it for backend wiring.

Frontend

The configuration form is metadata-driven. The UI calls GET /api/v1/organizations/telephony-providers/metadata, gets back the list of providers and their ProviderUIField definitions, and renders each form generically. No per-provider frontend code is needed — your ProviderUIMetadata declaration is what drives the form.

If you add a new field type that the existing renderer doesn't support (e.g. a file upload), extend the renderer in ui/src/app/(authenticated)/telephony-configurations/. The supported ProviderUIField.type values today are text, password, textarea, string-array, and number.

Audio Format Considerations

Each provider declares its wire format through its AudioConfig. Common shapes:

  • Twilio / Plivo: 8 kHz μ-law, base64-encoded JSON frames
  • Vonage: 16 kHz Linear PCM as binary frames
  • Asterisk ARI: 8 kHz Linear PCM via externalMedia
The pipeline sample rate is capped at 16 kHz to satisfy VAD; transports handle resampling between the wire format and the pipeline's internal rate.

Testing

# api/tests/telephony/test_your_provider.py
import pytest
from api.services.telephony.providers.your_provider import YourProvider

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_validate_config():
    provider = YourProvider({
        "api_key": "test_key",
        "api_secret": "test_secret",
        "from_numbers": ["+1234567890"],
    })
    assert provider.validate_config() is True

For end-to-end testing, save your provider through the telephony-configurations UI and trigger a test call from a workflow.

Best Practices

  1. Trust the registry — never import another provider's class directly; resolve through the factory helpers (get_default_telephony_provider, get_telephony_provider_by_id, etc.).
  2. Sensitive fields — mark every credential field sensitive=True in ProviderUIMetadata. The save endpoint masks these on read and preserves the original when the client re-submits a masked value.
  3. Inbound signature verification — always validate inbound webhook signatures in verify_inbound_signature. Returning True when no signature header is present is acceptable; return False when a signature is present but invalid.
  4. Transports load credentials lazily — call load_credentials_for_transport with the telephony_configuration_id from the workflow run. Don't read the org's default config from transport.py.
  5. Logging — use loguru.logger.

Reference Implementations

| Provider | Notable for | | --- | --- | | providers/twilio/ | Full-featured: outbound, inbound, conference transfers, status callbacks, custom strategies | | providers/plivo/ | Recently-added reference; mirrors Twilio's shape with multi-callback signatures | | providers/vonage/ | JWT auth, 16 kHz Linear PCM, NCCO responses | | providers/cloudonix/ | SIP-based, custom call strategies | | providers/telnyx/ | Call-control style: REST-driven inbound answer flow rather than markup response | | providers/ari/ | Minimal example — no routes.py, no inbound webhook verification, WebSocket-only |

Use ARI as the smallest viable example when your provider doesn't expose HTTP webhooks, and Twilio as the reference when it does.

documents.title: Channel Integrations
documents.excerpt: Connect messaging channels like WhatsApp, Telegram, and Instagram to handle conversations through your AI agents
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI supports multiple messaging channels through a unified channel configuration system. Each channel uses the same infrastructure — configure once, and your AI agents can handle both chat and voice interactions across all connected platforms.

Supported Channels

WhatsApp Cloud API for chat messaging and voice calling via Business Calling API Telegram Bot API for chat messaging Instagram Messaging API for direct messages

How Channels Work

All messaging channels follow the same pattern:

  1. Configure: Enter your channel credentials (API tokens, keys) in the Verasist UI under /channels
  2. Webhook Registration: Verasist provides a webhook URL that you register with the channel platform
  3. Inbound Messages: When a user sends a message, the platform sends a webhook to Verasist
  4. Agent Processing: Verasist routes the message to your AI agent's workflow
  5. Reply: The agent's response is sent back through the same channel

Shared Webhook Endpoint

Each channel type has its own webhook endpoint:

| Channel | Webhook URL | |---------|-------------| | WhatsApp | https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/whatsapp/webhook | | Telegram | https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/telegram/webhook | | Instagram | https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/instagram/webhook |

If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain.

Configuration

All channel configurations are managed from a single page:

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select the channel type (WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram)
  3. Enter the required credentials
  4. Save and register the webhook URL with the platform

Capabilities

| Channel | Chat | Voice | Webhook Auth | |---------|------|-------|-------------| | WhatsApp | ✅ | ✅ | X-Hub-Signature-256 (SHA-256 HMAC) | | Telegram | ✅ | ❌ | X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header | | Instagram | ✅ | ❌ | X-Hub-Signature-256 (SHA-256 HMAC) |

Troubleshooting

Webhook not receiving events- Verify the webhook URL is publicly accessible from the internet - Check that the webhook is registered correctly in the platform's developer dashboard - Ensure the channel configuration is saved in Verasist
Webhook verification failing- Confirm the verify token / webhook secret matches between Verasist and the platform - For Meta platforms (WhatsApp, Instagram), ensure the app secret is configured for signature validation - Check for proxy or load balancer modifications to the request
Messages not sending- Verify the access token / bot token is valid and not expired - Check that the target user ID is correct - Ensure the account has the necessary permissions (e.g., WhatsApp Business account verified)

documents.title: WhatsApp Integration
documents.excerpt: Connect your WhatsApp Business account to Verasist AI for chat messaging and voice calling
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI integrates with WhatsApp through Meta's Cloud API and Business Calling API. Once configured, your AI agents can:

  • Chat: Send and receive WhatsApp messages automatically
  • Voice: Make and receive WhatsApp voice calls via WebRTC
The WhatsApp integration uses Meta's Graph API infrastructure. All communication flows through Meta's servers — Verasist acts as the AI brain that processes messages and calls.

Prerequisites

  • A Meta Business App created in the Meta Developer Dashboard
  • A WhatsApp Business Account linked to your Meta app
  • A verified phone number for WhatsApp Business
  • The following credentials from Meta:
- Permanent Access Token — Generated from your Meta app's WhatsApp settings - Phone Number ID — The ID of your WhatsApp Business phone number - Verify Token — A custom token you create for webhook verification - App Secret (optional but recommended) — For webhook signature validation

Configuration

Step 1: Set Up Meta App

  1. Go to developers.facebook.com and create a new app (or use an existing one)
  2. Add the WhatsApp product to your app
  3. Under WhatsApp → API Setup, note your:
- Phone Number ID - WhatsApp Business Account ID
  1. Generate a Permanent Access Token from System Users or via the WhatsApp settings

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select WhatsApp as the channel type
  3. Fill in the credentials:
| Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | Name | A display name for this configuration (e.g. "WhatsApp Prod") | | Access Token | WhatsApp Cloud API permanent access token | | Phone Number ID | Your WhatsApp Business phone number ID from Meta | | Verify Token | A custom token for webhook verification — create any string and use the same value in Meta's webhook config | | App Secret | Meta App Secret from App Settings → Basic. Used for X-Hub-Signature-256 validation (recommended) | | Graph API Version | Meta Graph API version (default: v21.0) | | Enabled Capabilities | Select "Chat" and/or "Voice" |
  1. Click Save Configuration

Step 3: Register Webhook with Meta

  1. In your Meta app dashboard, go to WhatsApp → Configuration → Webhook
  2. Set the Callback URL to:
   https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/whatsapp/webhook
  1. Set the Verify Token to the same value you entered in Verasist
  2. Click Verify and Save
  3. Under Webhook Fields, subscribe to at least:
- messages — for incoming chat messages - message_template_status — if using templates
If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain. The webhook URL must be publicly accessible for Meta to send events.

Chat Messaging

Once configured, incoming WhatsApp messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a WhatsApp message to your business number
  2. Meta sends a webhook to Verasist with the message content
  3. Verasist matches the webhook to your organization and channel config
  4. Your AI agent's workflow processes the message and generates a reply
  5. The reply is sent back through the WhatsApp Cloud API

Voice Calling

WhatsApp voice calling uses Meta's Business Calling API (WebRTC-based):

  1. An outbound call is initiated from the Verasist UI or via API
  2. Verasist creates a WebRTC session through Meta's calling infrastructure
  3. Audio streams between the caller and your AI agent in real time
  4. The voice pipeline handles speech-to-text, LLM reasoning, and text-to-speech
To enable voice calling, select both Chat and Voice in the Enabled Capabilities field.
WhatsApp voice calling requires additional Meta business verification and approval. Refer to Meta's Business Calling API documentation for prerequisites and limitations.

Webhook Security

Verasist validates incoming WhatsApp webhooks using:

  1. Verify Token (hub.verify_token): Used during initial webhook registration (GET challenge)
  2. App Secret (X-Hub-Signature-256): SHA-256 HMAC signature of the request body. If configured, Verasist validates every POST webhook against this signature
It's strongly recommended to configure the App Secret for production use.

Inbound Message Flow

WhatsApp User → Meta Server → Webhook → Verasist → Agent Workflow → Reply → Meta API → WhatsApp User

The from_identity in the webhook payload is the user's WhatsApp phone number (e.g. +905321234567), which is used to track conversations and maintain context.

Test Your Integration

  1. Save your WhatsApp configuration in Verasist
  2. Register the webhook URL in Meta's dashboard and verify it succeeds
  3. Send a test WhatsApp message to your business number
  4. Check that your AI agent responds
  5. Check call logs in the Verasist dashboard for any errors

Troubleshooting

Webhook verification fails- Ensure the Verify Token in Verasist exactly matches the token set in Meta's webhook config - Confirm the callback URL is publicly accessible (Meta performs a GET request to it) - Check that your server's firewall allows inbound HTTPS traffic
Messages not being received- Verify you subscribed to the messages webhook field in Meta's dashboard - Check that the phone number is connected to your WhatsApp Business Account - Ensure the access token has whatsapp_business_messaging permission
Messages not sending- Verify the access token is still valid (not expired) - Check that the recipient's phone number is in the correct format - Ensure the WhatsApp Business account has not hit rate limits
Voice calls not connecting- Confirm "Voice" is enabled in the configuration's capabilities - Ensure the access token has whatsapp_business_voice permission - Verify the phone number supports voice calling (requires business verification)

documents.title: Telegram Integration
documents.excerpt: Connect your Telegram bot to Verasist AI for automated chat messaging
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI integrates with Telegram through the Telegram Bot API. Once configured, your AI agents can automatically handle Telegram conversations — answering questions, processing requests, and engaging users directly in Telegram chats.

The Telegram integration is chat-only (Telegram Bot API does not support public voice calling for bots).

Prerequisites

  • A Telegram bot created via @BotFather
  • Your bot's Bot Token (obtained from BotFather)
  • A publicly accessible server for webhook delivery (your Verasist instance)

Configuration

Step 1: Create a Telegram Bot

  1. Open Telegram and message @BotFather
  2. Send /newbot and follow the prompts to create your bot
  3. Save the Bot Token provided by BotFather (format: 123456789:ABCdefGHIjklMNOpqrsTUVwxyz)
  4. Optionally, set a profile picture and description with /setuserpic and /setdescription

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select Telegram as the channel type
  3. Fill in the credentials:
| Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | Name | A display name for this configuration (e.g. "Telegram Bot") | | Bot Token | Your Telegram bot token from @BotFather | | Webhook Secret Token | A custom secret for X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token validation (recommended) |
  1. Click Save Configuration

Step 3: Set the Webhook

Unlike Meta platforms, Telegram does not use a GET challenge for webhook verification. Instead, you register the webhook URL via the Bot API setWebhook method:

curl -X POST "https://api.telegram.org/bot/setWebhook" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/telegram/webhook",
    "secret_token": "YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET"
  }'

Replace:

  • with your bot token
  • YOUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET with the webhook secret you configured in Verasist
Verify the webhook was set:

curl "https://api.telegram.org/bot/getWebhookInfo"
If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain. The webhook URL must be publicly accessible (HTTPS required by Telegram).

How It Works

Once configured, incoming Telegram messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a message to your Telegram bot
  2. Telegram sends a webhook to Verasist with the message update
  3. Verasist validates the X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header (if configured)
  4. The webhook is matched to your organization and channel config
  5. Your AI agent's workflow processes the message and generates a reply
  6. The reply is sent back through the Telegram Bot API (sendMessage)

Message Flow

Telegram User → Telegram Server → Webhook → Verasist → Agent Workflow → Reply → Bot API → Telegram User

The from_identity used for conversation tracking is the user's Telegram chat_id.

Webhook Security

Verasist validates incoming Telegram webhooks using:

  • X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token header: If you set a webhook_secret in the Verasist configuration, every incoming webhook is validated against this header. Telegram includes this header in every webhook request if set during setWebhook.
It's strongly recommended to configure the webhook secret for production use.

Supported Update Types

The Telegram integration handles:

  • Text messages (message with text field)
  • Direct messages and group mentions (when the bot is mentioned with @botname)
Unsupported update types (ignored silently):
  • edited_message
  • callback_query
  • inline_query
  • Photos, videos, documents, and other non-text media
  • Channel posts

Test Your Integration

  1. Save your Telegram configuration in Verasist
  2. Run the setWebhook command to register your webhook URL
  3. Verify with getWebhookInfo — you should see "ok": true and "url" pointing to Verasist
  4. Send a message to your bot on Telegram
  5. Check that your AI agent responds
  6. Check the Verasist dashboard for any errors

Troubleshooting

Webhook not receiving events- Run getWebhookInfo to check if the webhook URL is set correctly - Verify the webhook URL uses HTTPS (Telegram requires HTTPS) - Ensure there are no pending updates: getWebhookInfo shows pending_update_count - Check that your server's firewall allows inbound HTTPS from Telegram's IPs
Secret token validation fails- Ensure the webhook_secret in Verasist matches the secret_token sent in setWebhook - Re-run setWebhook if you changed the secret
Bot not responding- Verify the bot token is valid and the bot is not blocked by the user - Check that there's at least one workflow in your organization - Ensure the workflow has an agent node configured - Check the Verasist logs for pipeline errors
Messages sending slowly- Telegram Bot API has rate limits (~30 messages/second per chat) - Check network latency between Verasist and api.telegram.org - The LLM inference time is the dominant factor in response latency

documents.title: Instagram Integration
documents.excerpt: Connect your Instagram Business account to Verasist AI for automated direct message handling
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist AI integrates with Instagram through Meta's Instagram Messaging API. Once configured, your AI agents can automatically respond to Instagram Direct Messages — handling customer inquiries, support requests, and engagement through your Instagram Business account.

The Instagram integration is chat-only (Instagram Messaging API does not support voice calling). It uses the same Meta Graph API infrastructure as WhatsApp, with graph.instagram.com as the API endpoint.

Prerequisites

  • A Meta Business App created in the Meta Developer Dashboard
  • An Instagram Business Account linked to a Facebook Page
  • The Instagram account must be connected to your Meta app
  • The following credentials from Meta:
- Access Token — Page or User access token with Instagram messaging permissions - Instagram Account ID (IGSID) — The Instagram-scoped ID for your business account - Verify Token — A custom token you create for webhook verification - App Secret (optional but recommended) — For webhook signature validation

Configuration

Step 1: Set Up Meta App for Instagram

  1. Go to developers.facebook.com and create a new app (or use an existing one)
  2. Add the Instagram product to your app
  3. Under Instagram settings, configure:
- Instagram Basic Display - Instagram Messaging API
  1. Connect your Instagram Business Account to a Facebook Page linked to your app
  2. Generate an Access Token with the following permissions:
- instagram_basic - instagram_manage_messages - pages_show_list - pages_messaging
  1. Note your Instagram Account ID (IGSID) from the Instagram settings page

Step 2: Configure in Verasist AI

  1. Navigate to /channels and click Add configuration
  2. Select Instagram as the channel type
  3. Fill in the credentials:
| Field | Description | |-------|-------------| | Name | A display name for this configuration (e.g. "Instagram DM Bot") | | Access Token | Instagram API permanent access token from Meta | | Instagram Account ID | Your Instagram Business Account ID (IGSID) from Meta | | Verify Token | A custom token for webhook verification — create any string and use the same value in Meta's webhook config | | App Secret | Meta App Secret from App Settings → Basic. Used for X-Hub-Signature-256 validation (recommended) | | Graph API Version | Meta Graph API version (default: v25.0) |
  1. Click Save Configuration

Step 3: Register Webhook with Meta

  1. In your Meta app dashboard, go to Instagram → Settings → Webhook
  2. Set the Callback URL to:
   https://api.verasist.ai/api/v1/channels/instagram/webhook
  1. Set the Verify Token to the same value you entered in Verasist
  2. Click Verify and Save
  3. Under Webhook Fields, subscribe to:
- messages — for incoming direct messages - messaging_postbacks — if using quick reply buttons
If you're self-hosting Verasist, replace api.verasist.ai with your own domain. The webhook URL must be publicly accessible for Meta to send events.

How It Works

Once configured, incoming Instagram Direct Messages are automatically routed to your AI agent:

  1. User sends a Direct Message to your Instagram Business account
  2. Meta sends a webhook to Verasist with the message content and IGSID
  3. Verasist validates the X-Hub-Signature-256 header (if App Secret is configured)
  4. The webhook is matched to your organization and channel config
  5. Your AI agent's workflow processes the message and generates a reply
  6. The reply is sent back through graph.instagram.com/messages

Message Flow

Instagram User → Meta Server → Webhook → Verasist → Agent Workflow → Reply → Instagram API → Instagram User

The from_identity used for conversation tracking is the sender's Instagram-scoped ID (IGSID). This is a numeric identifier unique to your app — it's different from the user's Instagram handle.

Webhook Security

Verasist validates incoming Instagram webhooks using the same pattern as WhatsApp:

  1. Verify Token (hub.verify_token): Used during initial webhook registration (GET challenge)
  2. App Secret (X-Hub-Signature-256): SHA-256 HMAC signature of the request body. If configured, Verasist validates every POST webhook against this signature
It's strongly recommended to configure the App Secret for production use.

Instagram vs WhatsApp

Both Instagram and WhatsApp use Meta's Graph API infrastructure, but they differ in a few important ways:

| Feature | Instagram | WhatsApp | |---------|-----------|----------| | API Endpoint | graph.instagram.com | graph.facebook.com | | User Identity | IGSID (numeric) | Phone number (E.164) | | Voice Calling | ❌ Not supported | ✅ Business Calling API | | Message Types | Text, media, quick replies | Text, media, templates, interactive | | API Version | v25.0 | v21.0 |

Limitations

  • No Voice: Instagram Messaging API does not support voice calling
  • 24-Hour Window: Meta enforces a 24-hour messaging window for free-form messages. After 24 hours, you may only send message templates
  • Business Account Required: A personal Instagram account cannot use the Messaging API — you must convert to a Business Account
  • App Review: For public access, your app must pass Meta's App Review

Test Your Integration

  1. Save your Instagram configuration in Verasist
  2. Register the webhook URL in Meta's dashboard and verify it succeeds
  3. Send a test Direct Message to your Instagram Business account
  4. Check that your AI agent responds
  5. Check the Verasist dashboard for any errors

Troubleshooting

Webhook verification fails- Ensure the Verify Token in Verasist exactly matches the token set in Meta's Instagram webhook config - Confirm the callback URL is publicly accessible (Meta performs a GET request to it) - Check that your Meta app has the Instagram product properly configured
Messages not being received- Verify you subscribed to the messages webhook field in Meta's dashboard - Check that the Instagram Business Account is properly connected to your Facebook Page - Ensure the access token has instagram_manage_messages permission - Confirm your app has passed Instagram's permissions review if in production mode
Messages not sending- Verify the access token is still valid (not expired) - Check the 24-hour messaging window — you may need a message template - Ensure the recipient IGSID is correct - Check Meta's rate limits for Instagram Messaging API
App review required- In development mode, only users with a role in your Meta app can message - For public access, submit your app for App Review with instagram_manage_messages permission - Ensure your privacy policy URL is configured in the Meta app settings

documents.title: MCP Server
documents.excerpt: Connect Codex, Claude, and other AI assistants to your Verasist workspace via the Model Context Protocol
documents.content:
Overview

Verasist exposes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI assistants like Codex, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and Cursor access your workspace and documentation. Once connected, an assistant can list your agents, fetch agent definitions, and search Verasist docs on your behalf.

Prerequisites

  • A Verasist API key. Generate one at /api-keys (or http://localhost:3010/api-keys for self-hosted). See API Keys.
  • Your Verasist MCP endpoint:
- Hosted: https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/ - Self-hosted: /api/v1/mcp/

The endpoint is also shown in Platform Settings → MCP Server inside the Verasist UI.

If you deployed Verasist to a remote server using setup_remote.sh, your endpoint is served with a self-signed SSL certificate. Claude Code will refuse MCP connections to it unless you start the CLI with TLS verification disabled: 
NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 claude

This is only required for self-signed certificates. If you have set up a custom domain with Let's Encrypt certificates via Certbot, no extra flag is needed.

Claude Code

Register Verasist as an MCP server with the Claude Code CLI:

claude mcp add --transport http verasist https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/ \
  --header "X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY"

Replace YOUR_API_KEY with the key you generated. For self-hosted deployments, swap the URL for your backend.

Verify the server is connected:

claude mcp list

Codex

Open Codex's config file (~/.codex/config.toml) and add a verasist MCP server:

[mcp_servers.verasist]
url = "https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/"
http_headers = { "X-API-Key" = "YOUR_API_KEY" }

Replace YOUR_API_KEY with the key you generated. For self-hosted deployments, replace the URL with your backend MCP endpoint.

If you prefer to keep the API key out of config.toml, store it in an environment variable instead:

[mcp_servers.verasist]
url = "https://app.verasist.ai/api/v1/mcp/"
env_http_headers = { "X-API-Key" = "VERASIST_API_KEY" }

Then set the API key before starting Codex:

export VERASIST_API_KEY="YOUR_API_KEY"
codex

Verify the server is registered:

codex mcp list
codex mcp get verasist

Claude Desktop

Open Claude Desktop's config file (claude_desktop_config.json) and add the verasist entry under mcpServers:

{
  "mcpServers": {

Cursor and other MCP clients

Any MCP client that supports Streamable HTTP transport can connect with the same URL and header. Paste the configuration above into your client's MCP settings file and replace YOUR_API_KEY.

Example prompts

Once the MCP server is connected, you can drive Verasist from your coding agent in plain English. A few prompts to try:

Explore your workspace

  • "List my agents in Verasist."
  • "Show me the definition of the agent called Lead Qualifier."
  • "Which credentials and tools are configured in my Verasist workspace?"
  • "List the recordings from my most recent agent."
Edit an agent
  • "In my Lead Qualifier agent, add a new agent node after the greeting that asks the caller for their budget, then routes to the existing qualification node."
  • "Add an end-call node to Support Bot that triggers when the user says they are done, with a polite goodbye prompt."
  • "Rename the intro node in Lead Qualifier to greeting and update any edges that reference it."
  • "Change the LLM model on all agent nodes in Support Bot to gpt-4o-mini."
Learn the platform
  • "Search the Verasist docs for how to configure a TURN server."
  • "What node types does Verasist support, and what fields does a knowledge_base node take?"
  • "How do I deploy Verasist on a custom domain with HTTPS?"
Agent edits are saved as a new draft version — your published agent keeps serving calls until you explicitly publish the draft from the Verasist UI.
The API key controls which workspace the assistant sees. Treat it like any other credential — do not commit it to source control or paste it into shared chats.
